items.title: 4.9-magnitude earthquake hits West Sikkim, mild tremors felt in Gangtok
items.summary:
A 4.9-magnitude earthquake struck the Sikkim-Nepal region early Thursday morning, triggering mild tremors in parts of West and Sikkim, including the state capital Gangtok.
Officials said there were no reports of property damage or casualties at the time of filing the copy.
The moderate earthquake occurred at 4.30 am, with its epicentre located around 40 km northwest of Yuksom in Gyalshing district of West Sikkim, according to the National Centre for Seismology (NCS).
The NCS said the earthquake was recorded at a depth of 73 km, at latitude 27.671 degrees north and longitude 87.987 degrees east.
Mild tremors were felt in several areas of West Sikkim, as well as parts of East Sikkim, including the state capital.

items.title: Oil below $92 amid hopes of peace talks
items.summary: Oil prices edged lower by more than $1 on Thursday as investors increasingly hopes for peace talks to resolve the Middle East conflict as well as the much-longer lasting Russia-Ukraine war.Brent crude futures fell more than $1 to trade below $92 per barrel, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures also lost over $1 to trade below $86 per barrel on Thursday morning. This comes after Brent crude rose over 1% on Wednesday after hitting two-month lows in the previous day.Russian and Ukrainian negotiators have agreed to a major prisoner exchange during their peace talks held over two days in Abu Dhabi, although US mediators said differences remained on other major issues, including territory. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said his country hoped to achieve concrete results on resolving the war this year.Also read | India's battered rupee finds an unlikely rescue party in cheaper oil and Wall Street's AI routBack in the Middle East, Iranian security chief Mohsen Rezaei said the government will not allow even a single particle of enriched nuclear material to leave Iran and there will be consequences if the US launches new strikes. The US meanwhile has said that nuclear issues must be part of any initial negotiations with Iran aimed at ending the eight-month-old war, while US officials downplayed the need for further military strikes.Meanwhile, OPEC+ crude oil production jumped in October, driven by a sharp increase in output from Saudi Arabia despite continued disruption to shipments through the Hormuz Strait. US crude stocks jumped by 9 million barrels in the latest week, Reuters quoted market sources as saying, citing data from the American Petroleum Institute.Where are oil prices heading for?While oil prices have dropped from their multi decade highs which they hit earlier this year, analysts remain cautious amid the seesaw political game in the Middle East. Goldman Sachs recently raised its oil price forecasts, citing increasing risks to global supplies. The investment bank warned that Brent crude could climb to $140 per barrel in 2027 if oil production across the Gulf region remains significantly below its 2025 average.Goldman Sachs recently raised its oil price forecasts, citing increasing risks to global supplies. The investment bank warned that Brent crude could climb to $140 per barrel in 2027 if oil production across the Gulf region remains significantly below its 2025 average.Also read | India in a 'sweet spot' amid oil volatility and currency dynamics: Kotak Neo's Anindya BanerjeeIn an upside scenario, Brent crude could reach $140 per barrel and average around $130 in 2027 if Gulf oil production remains 3.5 million barrels per day below its 2025 average, Reuters reported, citing Goldman Sachs' projections.Goldman Sachs expects oil markets to incorporate a higher geopolitical risk premium, given the possibility of disruptions to Middle Eastern supplies, the historical duration of major supply shocks and the challenges involved in securing a lasting diplomatic breakthrough.JPMorgan analysts also highlighted the uncertainty surrounding the conflict, saying it remained difficult to predict how the war would unfold. At the outset, the bank had expected the US administration to avoid crossing certain economic thresholds. Indians buy 30% more gold after recent price correction
items.summary: Kolkata: Indians stepped up purchases of precious metals during the Dhanteras-Diwali period despite elevated prices, with gold buying rising 30% by volume and silver demand increasing 10% over the same period last year, according to the India Bullion and Jewellers Association (IBJA). Jewellers said this signalled a revival of demand ahead of the crucial wedding season.As per the industry body, consumers bought 52 tonnes of gold worth ₹72,000 crore and 300 tonnes of silver valued at ₹5,400 crore during this year's Dhanteras-Diwali. The surge came after gold prices corrected from a peak of around ₹1.8 lakh to ₹1.42 lakh per 10 grams, encouraging buyers to return to the market. Advance purchases for the wedding season, which begins in mid-November and continues until March, also contributed to the increase.135751520"Jewellers have made good business in this year's Dhanteras and Diwali," said IBJA national secretary Surendra Mehta.There was a pent-up demand in the market, after many consumers had earlier halted purchases following Prime Minister Narendra Modi's appeal not to buy gold, he said. "Consumers had stayed away from the precious metal. But since the price has fallen and there is a chance of prices moving northwards again as Brent crude prices have fallen, people have come out to buy gold. In fact, buying is still continuing ."The timing of the festivals also supported purchases, with Dhanteras falling on November 6 and Diwali on November 8, both at the beginning of the month when most salaried people receive their salaries and festive bonus."This has resulted in healthy cash flow in the market, encouraging consumers to shop enthusiastically. Gold prices have also been relatively lower over the past four to six months, further improving purchasing sentiment," said Rajesh Rokde, chairman of the All India Gem & Jewellery Domestic Council. This fiscal year till September, gold sales by volume fell by almost 50% due to price and import duty increase, and PM Modi's call to avoid purchase of gold.Read more: Smallcap mutual fund inflows drop 29% MoM to Rs 6,407 crore in October. Should investors be cautious or continue investing?Gold has delivered substantial returns over the past few years, with prices rising from around ₹60,000 per 10 gm in 2023 to ₹80,000 in 2024, ₹1.15-1.20 lakh in 2025 and about ₹1.42 lakh this year during the Dhanteras-Diwali period. Silver too has witnessed significant appreciation. items.title: Debt Mutual Funds: What investors should know before investing
items.summary: Debt mutual funds saw a net outflow of Rs 1.8 lakh crore in September, the highest monthly withdrawal in the first half of FY27. Despite this, they remain an important investment avenue for investors looking to park surplus money, manage short-term goals and diversify their portfolios. A look at how debt funds work and what investors should know before investing.WHAT ARE DEBT MUTUAL FUNDS?Debt mutual funds invest in fixed-income instruments such as government securities, treasury bills, corporate bonds, commercial paper and certificates of deposit. They aim to provide relatively stable returns while taking lower risk than equity funds. Debt funds generate returns in two ways. The first is through the interest earned on the bonds and other securities held in the portfolio. The second comes from changes in bond prices. When bond prices rise, fund managers can book gains by selling these securities.HOW SHOULD INVESTORS CHOOSE A DEBT FUND? The choice depends on the investment horizon, liquidity needs and ability to tolerate fluctuations in returns. Investors looking to park money for a few days or months may consider overnight or liquid funds. Those with a horizon of six months to two years may look at ultra-short duration, low duration or money-market funds. For investment horizons of three years or more, categories such as short-duration funds, corporate bond funds and banking & PSU debt funds may be suitable. Gilt funds and long-duration funds are generally more appropriate for investors who understand interest-rate cycles.Read more: Smallcap mutual fund inflows drop 29% MoM to Rs 6,407 crore in October. Should investors be cautious or continue investing?WHY DID DEBT FUNDS WITNESS LARGE OUTFLOWS IN SEPTEMBER? The large outflows were largely driven by liquidity requirements rather than a change in investor appetite for debt funds. These schemes are widely used by companies and institutional investors to park surplus cash for short periods. September is also a quarter-end month when companies usually withdraw money to meet working capital requirements, advance tax payments and other financial obligations.Read more: Debt mutual funds see sharp recovery in October as quarter-end outflows reverseARE DEBT FUNDS RISK-FREE? While debt funds are generally less volatile than equity funds, they are not risk-free. One key risk is interest-rate risk. When interest rates rise, bond prices fall, which can affect the value of a fund’s portfolio. The second is credit risk, which arises when a company or other issuer fails to repay its debt or interest on time. Funds investing in lower-rated corporate bonds generally carry higher credit risk.HOW DO INTEREST RATES AFFECT DEBT FUND RETURNS? Interest rates and bond prices move in opposite directions. When interest rates fall, existing bonds offering higher interest become more attractive to investors. As demand for these bonds rises, their prices generally move up. This, in turn, tends to benefit debt funds. When interest rates rise, bond prices usually decline, which can weigh on returns. Long-duration funds are usually more affected by interest-rate changes, while liquid and overnight funds tend to see smaller fluctuations.

items.title: US stocks: S&P, Nasdaq end over 1% higher as AI-fueled optimism weighs
items.summary: The S&P 500 and the tech-heavy Nasdaq rose more than 1% on Wednesday after strong earnings from neocloud company CoreWeave eased concerns about excessive spending on artificial intelligence infrastructure. Nvidia also recovered some ground following a sharp two-session sell-off.The S&P 500 gained 96.91 points, or 1.29%, to end at 7,617.84 points, while the Nasdaq Composite gained 398.70 points, or 1.59%, to 25,464.57. The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 245.03 points, or 0.47%, to 52,476.92.Battered CoreWeave shares surged more than 20% to the highest intraday level in nearly two weeks. The company said it would become profitable in the first half of 2028 on an adjusted basis, seeking to reassure investors that strong demand and customer commitments could support its debt-fueled expansion.The results lifted other AI infrastructure stocks, with Nebius Group climbing 17.4% and Applied Digital gaining 8.6%.Nvidia rose 3.8% after losing about $430 billion in market value over the previous two sessions. Its shares had come under pressure amid reports concerning CEO Jensen Huang’s relationship with a businesswoman alleged to have ties to Chinese intelligence.The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index jumped 7% to a one-week high. Marvell Technology surged 12.2%, while Micron Technology gained 13.3%.Equity markets have swung sharply this week as concerns about slower data-centre development, higher interest rates and uncertainty surrounding Nvidia compete with investors’ appetite to buy the dip.Investors purchased equities during last week’s sell-off, with all net inflows coming through exchange-traded funds and institutional clients leading the buying, Bank of America Global Research analysts said in a note.“We’ve seen some of the leverage getting washed out post the midterms, which could set us up for a constructive year-end rally,” said Ron Albahary, chief investment officer at Laird Norton Wetherby.Six of the 11 major S&P 500 sectors traded higher, led by technology and energy.The CBOE Volatility Index, widely known as Wall Street’s fear gauge, declined for a fourth consecutive session to 17.7.Investors also assessed the terms of Anthropic’s blockbuster initial public offering. The Claude chatbot developer is seeking a valuation of as much as $1.4 trillion.“There’s a lot of optimistic expectations related to Anthropic’s business ... any disappointment related to earnings growth, which has been outsized, could cause a selloff within the AI trade itself,” Albahary said.Rate concerns persistHotter-than-expected inflation data released on Tuesday strengthened expectations that the Federal Reserve would raise interest rates next month. Traders now fully price in a December increase, according to CME FedWatch.Before the CPI report, Fed Governor Christopher Waller said policymakers should consider raising rates by 50 basis points if October inflation accelerated. He warned that a smaller move could damage the central bank’s inflation-fighting credibility.Oil prices rose 2.8% after Iran’s security chief said Tehran would not allow enriched nuclear material to leave the country.The US bond market was closed on Wednesday for Veterans Day.(Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies. These do not represent the views of The Economic Times)

items.title: CoreWeave shares surge over 26%, spark rally in battered AI cloud stocks
items.summary: CoreWeave shares surged more than 26% on Wednesday, fuelling a rally in battered AI cloud stocks after heavy infrastructure spending delivered strong revenue growth and the company signalled a retreat from the borrowing spree that had raised fears of an artificial intelligence bubble, Reuters reported.CoreWeave shares were trading at $61.61, up $12.88 or 26.43% over the previous close.The results also helped lift Nvidia, a major CoreWeave backer, by 2%. Nvidia had fallen sharply over the previous two sessions amid uncertainty surrounding CEO Jensen Huang following reports about his relationship with a Chinese businesswoman alleged to have ties to Beijing’s intelligence apparatus.Shares of other so-called neocloud companies, including Nebius and Iren, also rallied after weeks of pressure. Investors have worried that their debt-funded data-centre expansion could backfire if demand for AI computing weakens.For live updates on US Markets, click here“CoreWeave’s earnings directly addressed the fear that’s driven this whole selloff,” said Dan Sheehan, director of portfolio management at Telos Wealth Advisors, according to Reuters. “The neocloud that became the poster child for AI financing worries took real weight off the fear that had been the heart of the selloff.”Democrats’ sweep of last week’s US midterm elections had further unsettled the industry. Several victorious candidates campaigned for stricter regulation and moratoriums on new data-centre construction, including in Texas, a key market for the sector.CoreWeave CEO Michael Intrator told Reuters on Tuesday that increased regulatory scrutiny could slow data-centre development across the industry. However, he did not expect it to significantly affect the company’s expansion plans or raise costs.Intrator said CoreWeave’s planned capacity additions over the next year would remain unaffected.Also Read: Is AI wheel broken? Julius Baer flags 3 variables shaping AI investments ahead of Anthropic IPOThe company also said it would avoid unsecured debt markets following a recent surge in borrowing costs. Cash flow from existing contracts would cover repayments on both current and future debt, it added—a financing plan analysts described as credible.“CoreWeave delivered about the best quarter we could have asked for. Stats were good-to-great, funding concerns were addressed and the strategic moves make sense,” Bernstein analysts led by Madison Rezaei said in a client note.However, they warned that CoreWeave “will be among the first and hardest hit” once the shortage of AI computing capacity eases.The risks of mistiming AI investments were evident on Tuesday when SoftBank recorded a $3.7 billion write-down on non-refundable payments for equipment intended to power its US data centres. The charge contributed to a second-quarter net loss of $7 billion, the company’s first in nearly two years.Uncertainty surrounding Huang has also weighed on the AI sector. The controversy intensified on Tuesday after reports alleged that his relationship helped facilitate billions of dollars in Nvidia chip shipments to China.Republican US Senator Kevin Cramer, a member of the Senate Banking Committee, called on Huang to step down as Nvidia CEO.For now, CoreWeave’s results have given AI infrastructure investors some relief. Nebius, Iren, Oracle and Applied Digital climbed between 6% and 14%.With the exception of Nebius, the stocks had fallen between 32% and 48% this year through Tuesday. Nebius, by contrast, had gained 60%.Together, the companies—including CoreWeave—were on track to add about $36 billion in market value if the gains held. Nvidia alone was positioned to gain nearly $100 billion.Nebius is scheduled to report its results before Thursday’s opening bell.(Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies. These do not represent the views of The Economic Times)

items.title: Nvidia rebounds after $480 billion wipeout
items.summary: Nvidia stock (NVDA) surged nearly 4% in premarket trading on Wednesday, November 11, as investors bought the dip after a two-day sell-off that wiped roughly $480 billion from the chipmaker's market value. Shares rose to $175.45 at 6:49 a.m. ET, up 3.88%, after closing Tuesday at $168.89, down $9.78, or 5.47%.The rebound came alongside gains in US stock futures, with Nasdaq 100 futures rising 1.67%, S&P 500 futures gaining 0.74% and Dow futures edging up 0.03%.Investors are returning to AI stocks even as Nvidia faces an investigation involving CEO Jensen Huang, just six days before its November 17 earnings report.Why is Nvidia stock rising today after a $480 billion market value crash?Nvidia's rebound comes after two difficult trading sessions. Shares fell 4.3% on Monday and another 5.47% on Tuesday as investors reacted to reports about Huang's relationship with a woman suspected by US intelligence of having links to Chinese intelligence.The stock closed Monday at $178.67 before falling to $168.89 on Tuesday. Wednesday's premarket recovery has helped Nvidia regain part of those losses, although shares remain below their level before the controversy intensified.The recovery is also part of a broader rally in AI stocks. CoreWeave shares gained more than 10% in premarket trading after its quarterly results helped ease concerns about AI infrastructure spending. Micron and Marvell also rose nearly 7%.Nvidia faces Jensen Huang investigation as board hires outside law firmNvidia confirmed on Tuesday that its independent directors had hired Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to investigate whether company secrets or US national security had been compromised.The investigation will be led by former acting US Attorney Joon H. Kim.The company had already announced an independent review on Sunday. Nvidia's board said it had no reason to believe that company secrets or national security had been compromised. It also expressed confidence in Huang and his leadership team.The allegations remain unproven, and China has denied claims of an espionage operation.Huang returned to Nvidia's office on Monday and continued holding meetings on Tuesday, according to CNBC. His return comes as investors assess whether the controversy could affect Nvidia's operations or leadership.Bank of America warns Nvidia could face three different outcomesBank of America outlined three possible scenarios for Nvidia in a research note on Tuesday.The first involves a contained investigation with no major disruption to leadership. Under this outcome, investor attention could return to Nvidia's earnings and AI chip demand.The second involves prolonged uncertainty that puts pressure on the company's valuation ahead of its quarterly results.The third carries greater financial risks. Bank of America analyst Vivek Arya warned that adverse findings, leadership changes or tighter restrictions could require investors to reassess Nvidia's earnings outlook.Morgan Stanley removes Nvidia stock from top picks after 25% declineMorgan Stanley removed Nvidia from its top stock picks on Wednesday after shares dropped more than 25% since the bank added the company to its list on October 2.The bank's analysts said Huang's leadership remains crucial to Nvidia's strategic direction.The decision adds to concerns about how much Nvidia's market valuation depends on its chief executive.Zacks Chief Equity Strategist John Blank also warned that investors were concerned about possible additional US restrictions and further developments in the investigation.Speaking to CNBC, Blank said the situation was negative for Nvidia, Huang and the broader AI trade.Nvidia earnings on November 17: Can NVDA stock sustain its recovery?Nvidia's next quarterly earnings report is scheduled for November 17, giving investors another major event to watch.The market will focus on revenue growth, AI chip demand, profit margins and the company's guidance for the coming quarter.

items.title: UK firm to invest 250 mln pounds in India
items.summary: New Delhi, UK-based business financial platform Tide plans to invest around 250 million pounds (about Rs 3,100 crore) in India by the end of 2030 to scale up operations and technology centres supporting its global business.The company plans to ramp up investment up to 500 million pounds in the longer term.India will remain an important part of its global operations, with investments focused on strengthening its operations and technology centres that support its businesses in the UK and Europe, Tide said in a statement.Tide employs around 800 people at its centre of excellence in Hyderabad across functions such as member support, product and engineering.The Hyderabad centre accounts for nearly one-third of the company's total workforce and drives its core operations, engineering and product innovation, it said, adding that the company also intends to advance its operations centre in Delhi, which supports its UK and European businesses.However, it said, following a detailed strategic review, Tide concluded that the economics of its India member-facing business did not offer a viable path to sustainable profitability, despite having grown to more than one million members in the country since December 2022.It will, therefore, focus its investments on the UK and European markets, where it sees greater potential for profitable growth at scale.The decision to wind down the India member-facing business will affect around 400 employees, it said.The company would support the affected employees during the transition, including offering transfers to its global operations and technology centres wherever possible, it said, adding that the company will also communicate directly with its members in India regarding the implications of the decision.Tide Chief Executive Officer Oliver Prill said India remained an integral part of the company's global business and long-term growth plans.The company has built a significant operations and technology presence in India and intends to continue expanding these capabilities, he said in the statement.Prill said the decision to exit the member-facing business followed a strategic review which found that the economics of the proposition did not provide a sustainable path to profitability, particularly compared with opportunities in the UK and Europe.Tide expects its annualised revenue run rate to exceed USD 500 million in the coming months.The UK remains its largest and most established market, where the company is profitable and approaching one million small and medium enterprise (SME) members, equivalent to around 16 per cent of the market.It also plans to leverage artificial intelligence (AI) to improve operational efficiency, enhance its products and provide better support to members.

Mahindra & Mahindra (M&M) and Ola Electric Mobility emerged among the top gainers in the sector, with the former leading the rally with an intra-day gain of nearly 5%.M&M climbed 4.81% to touch an intra-day high of Rs 3,449, while Ola Electric Mobility advanced 3.53% to Rs 35.16.Hyundai Motor India was another major gainer, rising 3.08% to an intra-day high of Rs 2,175, while TVS Motor Company gained 2.89% to Rs 4,636.10. Ather Energy advanced 2.40% to Rs 1,904.50.Among other automobile companies, Maruti Suzuki India rose 2.10% to Rs 13,199, while Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles gained 2.03% to Rs 301. JBM Auto advanced 2% to Rs 511.95, while Bajaj Auto registered the lowest gain among the nine stocks, rising 1.28% to Rs 11,120.At the last check, M&M was trading 4.5% higher, followed by TVS Motor Company, which was up 2.53%. Ola Electric Mobility gained 2.20%, while Hyundai Motor India advanced 2.3%. Maruti Suzuki India was up 2%, while Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles and Ather Energy gained 1.5% each. Bajaj Auto and JBM Auto were trading 0.5% higher each, while Ashok Leyland was flat.ALSO READ: Earnings recovery, FII revival: 5 factors that will shape Dalal Street's next move after Q2What does the Centre's new EV procurement policy say?The Department of Expenditure (DEA), under the Ministry of Finance, has revised the Net Dealer Price (NDP) ceiling for the procurement of staff cars by government ministries and departments, doubling the limit for electric vehicles to Rs 20 lakh from Rs 10 lakh for internal combustion engine (ICE) vehicles.Under the revised instructions, electric vehicles have been made the default choice for government staff-car procurement. Ministries and departments are directed to ordinarily procure EVs when purchasing or replacing their existing staff cars.However, the revised instructions do not completely prohibit the purchase of conventional vehicles. items.summary: Tehran: Iran's army said Wednesday that an oil tanker had struck a mine and caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz, where the country has been targeting ships that transit without its authorisation.Since the outbreak of the Middle East war in late February, Tehran has heavily restricted traffic through the strategic waterway, insisting vessels use routes authorised by the Islamic republic.The United States has in response imposed a naval blockade on Iranian ports and helped tankers travel the strait, which normally carries about one-fifth of global oil.The American military recently claimed all mines had been cleared from the strait."Early this morning, a violating oil tanker caught fire after striking a naval mine in an unsafe, prohibited area in the east of the Strait of Hormuz," the naval forces of Iran's army said in a statement carried by state TV.In recent weeks Tehran has made multiple announcements saying ships had caught fire in the strait, often claiming they struck mines.US Central Command, which oversees US military operations in the region, has been escorting ships through the waterway and said last month that it had helped Gulf countries export 1.5 billion barrels of oil via Hormuz since the summer.On Tuesday, the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, the ideological arm of Iran's military, said three other oil tankers had caught fire in the strait.

items.summary: Michael Burry is known for his bearish take on artificial intelligence-linked stocks, but the ‘Big Short’ investor dismissed worries around Nvidia following the controversy surrounding CEO Jensen Huang’s extramarital affair, calling the chipmaker a “heck of a trade”.The popular American investor sees potential for a near-term trading opportunity in Nvidia but doubts the controversy surrounding CEO Jensen Huang will damage Nvidia's business much. "Still, I believe Nvidia's competitive advantage will shrink over the next five years," he said. While Burry struck a positive note for Nvidia, he is not exactly bullish on the chipmaker. He is not tempted to make a long-term trade on the stock, but he feels the entire market will soon think it is a “heck of a trade.”Also read | Nvidia Stock Sell-Off Deepens: Spy scandal, price target cuts put AI giant under pressureAll about Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's affair controversy Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang openly admitted that he has been in an intimate relationship with a business executive whom US intelligence reportedly alleged was a Chinese spy, leading to the company launching an investigation into the reports. This has led to a sharp selloff in Nvidia shares, wiping out around $430 billion from its market value in just two sessions.Huang, in a message to company employees released on Sunday, acknowledged having an affair and apologised to both his family and company staff. "I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry,” the 63-year-old Taiwanese-born executive said.Also read | Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang faces leadership questions as Republican senator calls for his resignationMichael Burry takes U-turn on Nvidia?Notably, Michael Burry had been shorting Nvidia shares until September, when he announced that he is exiting some of the put options. Put options typically reflect a trader’s conviction that the stock price is about to fall. Burry had long held put options on a variety of stocks which remained the face of the AI boom, spooking investors about a possible market crash when the artificial intelligence frenzy fizzles out. The American investor later exited some of the put options, triggering some optimism, but Burry clarified that it was not his intention.Burry said he sold his December 2026 puts on both Nvidia and Palantir entirely to avoid rapid time-based decay. He added that he did not replace or roll the positions, saying he is "pulling back on exposures across the portfolio." Michael Burry's AI warningsThe American investor who famously correctly predicted the 2008 US housing crisis has been sounding the alarm since the beginning of the year over a prospective big market crash when the AI frenzy fizzles out. Earlier this year, Burry said he continues to believe that the market is close to a major top, warning of a similar crash to that of 1987 when Dow Jones recorded a historic 23% plunge, which led to the introduction of regulatory circuit breakers. However, the market investor noted that the S&P 500 making new highs likely will bring new money into the market.He wrote in a Substack post that he sees many indicators, both technical and fundamental, lining up for the same conclusion as the Dotcom crash. "1999 went where no market had gone before, and I would say so can this one...It is already there on several indicators," he said, arguing that massive venture capital flows, rising AI debt issuance, and extreme market optimism are creating conditions where valuations may detach from economic reality.Also read | Anthropic retracts details of $69 billion IPO filing sent to bankers. Why analysts are raising worries over valuationsBurry’s popular bet against the housing market was depicted in the 2015 movie titled 'The Big Short', which starred Christian Bale, Ryan Gosling, Steve Carell and others.Disclaimer: This article has been written by Debaroti Adhikary, who is not a SEBI-registered Research Analyst or an Investment Adviser. items.title: Hijack threat note found on Air India flight, plane taken to isolation bay
items.summary:
A hijack threat note found in the washroom of a Mumbai-bound Air India flight before take-off on Wednesday morning prompted security officials to park the aircraft in an isolation bay of the airport here, an official said.
The flight was scheduled to depart at 10.20 am.
The note threatening that the plane would be hijacked at 11.10 am was found in the washroom just before the departure of the flight, Kolkata airport director Vikram Singh said.
All the passengers who had boarded the aircraft were deboarded, and it was taken to the isolation bay, he said.
Security protocols were immediately activated, and the aircraft was moved to an isolation bay for a thorough inspection and necessary precautionary measures, he said.

items.title: China builds inside Europe's walls
items.summary: Sofia: China doesn't need to clear Europe's trade barriers. It can build inside them.Chinese companies are establishing production and supplier networks across Central and Eastern Europe, which could enable them to gain more control over the technologies and inputs that European manufacturing needs.China is increasingly challenging the European Union in the advanced manufacturing sectors that helped the EU weather the first China shock, which reshaped global manufacturing in the 2000s. Chinese firms are competing with the EU in chemicals, machinery, advanced equipment and autos - and increasingly coming out on top on both price and quality.The EU trade deficit with China has nearly quadrupled over the past decade, from around €100 billion in 2014 to over €370 billion in 2025, or roughly €1 billion a day, according to Eurostat data.France and Germany are seeking to push back with stronger trade defences, but import curbs will achieve little if Chinese investment, ownership and control of critical technologies recreates the same vulnerabilities inside the single market.LOOKING EASTCentral and Eastern Europe appear to be key to China's growth strategy in Europe.While the EU's trade deficit with China has hovered around 2% of EU gross domestic product (GDP) since 2014, it has risen sharply in parts of CEE. For example, Slovenia's goods deficit with China rose from 2.5% to 16% over that period. Meanwhile, Poland's goods deficit surged from €8.9 billion to €34.3 billion, equivalent to about 5.2% of GDP. The Czech Republic's deficit nearly quadrupled to €22 billion, or roughly 8% of GDP, and Hungary's tripled to €10.4 billion, or about 6% of GDP.Investment and corporate ties deepened that exposure. In 2025, Chinese foreign direct investment (FDI) flows into the EU approached €16.8 billion, and the cumulative value of Chinese investment in the bloc was about €95 billion, according to Eurostat and Rhodium Group data.While most legacy Chinese FDI in Europe centered on Germany, France and the Benelux countries, the focus has shifted east in recent years. CEE has attracted more than half of Chinese FDI into the EU and Britain since 2021, according to an analysis by the Rhodium Group, with an even larger regional share when the Western Balkans are included. Hungary has attracted the largest share of new investment since the COVID-19 pandemic, hitting 44% in 2023 and 23% in 2025.The investment surge in CEE has largely been driven by mega-projects in the electric vehicle (EV) supply chain. Chinese EV and battery manufacturers CATL, BYD and Sunwoda are all establishing major Hungarian operations. Slovakia has attracted investment from Chinese battery tech firm Gotion, and will be the site of a new Volvo plant owned by the Chinese automaker Geely.Meanwhile, Serbia, which has significant steel and copper assets, has signed contracts with Chinese auto firms Minth , Shanghai Automotive Chassis (SHAC), BMTS Technology and Xingyu Automotive, envisaging around €1 billion in investment and nearly 1,700 car-parts jobs, according to the government. The deals also include a new robotics factory in Sabac, billed as Europe's first humanoid robot mass production base.These investments can create jobs, spur growth, and accelerate the energy transition, but they may also erode EU competitiveness over time. Outsourcing key advanced manufacturing technologies to Chinese entities risks deepening Europe's dependence on external supply chains and weakening domestic innovation and R&D.DEFEND, THEN COMPETEEurope is seeking to limit China's access to its consumer markets and industries, but the current Franco-German push for faster defensive trade action and tougher investment screening across the bloc appears to be too little too late.Europe's flagship proposal, the Industrial Accelerator Act, leaves manufacturers' key competitiveness gaps unaddressed. Moreover, its screening mechanism would largely leave unexamined Chinese control via ultimate ownership, foreign subsidies and supply-chain concentration - some key issues when looking at CEE's growing dependence.There is also the problem of fragmentation across the bloc. Investment deals might be in one country's interest but could weaken the bloc's collective negotiating position with Beijing. To address this, the continent would likely need a permanent European economic security coordination mechanism to unite trade, competition and national screening authorities that could identify risks before investments become irreversible.Yet the chances of forming such a body at a time of growing political fragmentation within EU countries seem slim.And, ultimately, protectionism can only get Europe so far. It cannot compensate for the region's structural problems, including expensive energy, fragmented capital markets and slow industrial innovation. For that, the region would likely need to create a true energy union and invest in technological innovation. Building trade walls buys time, but not true change.(The views expressed here are those of Martin Vladimirov, director of the Geoeconomics Program of the Center for the Study of Democracy (CSD))

items.title: Dubai-bound tanker hit in Gulf; Indians injured
items.summary: A Dubai-bound oil tanker carrying six Indian seafarers was hit by a projectile while transiting the Persian Gulf on Tuesday, leaving four crew members injured, including one Indian national, the government said on Wednesday.Union Minister of Ports, Shipping and Waterways Sarbananda Sonowal identified the vessel as the Liberian-flagged very large crude carrier (VLCC) MT Fujairah Energy, which was travelling from Al Ruwais to Dubai."The remaining 18 crew members, including five other Indian seafarers, are safe and accounted for," Sonowal said on X.— sarbanandsonwal (@sarbanandsonwal) He even added that the government was in contact with the ship management company to ensure medical assistance and the safety of the affected seafarers."We are continuously monitoring the situation and remain in close contact with the ship management company to ensure the ongoing security, medical care and wellbeing of our seafarers," he wrote on X.The incident adds to concerns over the safety of commercial shipping and Indian seafarers in the Persian Gulf and surrounding waters, where vessels have faced repeated attacks.Last month, a Panama-flagged tanker, MT Louise 1, carrying 27 Indian seafarers was hit by limpet mines in the Strait of Hormuz, triggering a fire. The incident occurred 25 nautical miles (46 km) northeast of Oman's Khasab. The government subsequently confirmed that all Indian crew members were safe.Shipping routes, including the Strait of Hormuz, have faced disruptions and attacks since the Iran-US war began in February 2026.According to data from the Washington Institute for Near East Policy, 37 ships were attacked in October, the highest monthly total since the conflict began. US forces are also continuing to enforce a naval blockade of Iranian ports, adding to tensions in the region.

items.title: HEG Advanced Materials shares gain 5% after subsidiary secures Rs 610 crore incentive under ECMS
items.summary: Shares of HEG Advanced Materials gained 5% on Wednesday to an intraday high of Rs 305 on NSE after its subsidiary TACC received the approval letter for an incentive of Rs 609.50 crore under the Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme (ECMS) of the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology.According to a filing with the exchange, the company said that the incentive is for TACC’s Synthetic Graphite Anode Material project at Sirsoda Industrial Area, Dewas, Madhya Pradesh, and is subject to scheme guidelines and prescribed conditions.The Dewas facility is spread across more than 100 acres and is planned for a committed scaled capacity of beyond 30,000 metric tonnes per annum (MTPA) by FY2028-29. The first phase of 20,000 MTPA is targeted for commissioning by June 2027.Also Read |Kalyan Jewellers shares zoom 10%, hit upper circuit after strong Q2 earnings. What analysts are saying“We are grateful to the Government of India and the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology for this support, and for their vision of building a strong electronics component manufacturing base in the country,” said Riju Jhunjhunwala, Chairman, Managing Director and CEO, HEG Advanced Materials.“The approval under ECMS is a strong endorsement of TACC’s technology and of our belief that India can build a globally competitive battery materials value chain at home. Anode material sits at the heart of every battery cell, and producing it at scale in India is central to a secure and resilient energy storage supply chain,” Jhunjhunwala further said.The company also said that the approval strengthens HEG Advanced Materials’ vision, through its wholly owned subsidiary TACC to build localized, resilient and globally competitive battery materials value chain and it is also a significant step towards strengthening India’s advanced energy storage ecosystem.“The support under ECMS strengthens our ability to execute at scale. Our Dewas facility is designed to deliver high performance synthetic graphite anode material that meets the standards of global cell manufacturers,” said Ankur Khaitan, Managing Director and CEO, TACC.Khaitan also said that, “Our focus now is on timely execution, consistent quality and close collaboration with customers to ensure supply reliability. We thank the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology for its support.”What is Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme (ECMS)?According to the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, the main objective of the scheme is to develop a robust component manufacturing ecosystem by attracting investments (global / domestic) across the value chain by integrating its domestic electronic industry with the Global Value Chains (GVCs).The scheme provides differentiated fiscal incentives on target segment products in terms of turnover. Firstly, turnover linked incentive which is for six years with one year of gestation period. Secondly, capex incentive which is for five years and lastly, hybrid incentive which is a combination of turnover linked and capex incentive.HEG Advanced Materials Q2 updatesOn November 3, the company announced its Q2FY27 updates and said that it reported consolidated revenue from continuing operations of Rs 429.94 crore, total income of Rs 546.59 crore, EBITDA of Rs 312.78 crore and profit after tax of Rs 208.89 crore.While mentioning its business highlights, the company said that the advanced materials (TACC) which is Global lithium-ion battery production is expected to grow from about 2.3 TWh in 2025 to about 8 TWh by 2035, with non-China anode demand set to exceed 1 Mn tons by 2030 as cell makers diversify their supply chains.Also Read | HDFC Bank shares jump 17% in 10 days; analysts see private lender nearing an inflection point. Time to buy or wait?REPLUS has deployed over 1 GWh of energy storage capacity across BESS, electric mobility, telecom power solutions and hybrid energy applications. Alongside its operational 1 GWh Giga Factory in Pune, a 5 GWh highspeed, fully automatic prismatic line expansion facility is under construction, which will take total manufacturing capacity to 6 GWh on completion.The Green Power Businesses have a combined hydroelectric installed capacity of 278 MW in Himachal Pradesh, through the 86 MW Malana Power Company Limited project (MPCL) and the 192 MW AD Hydro Power Limited project, along with a 14 MW wind power project in Maharashtra (under HEGAM).HEG Advanced Materials share priceIn the last one week, the stock has gained over 4%, and nearly 29% in the last one month. items.summary: IIFL Finance shares rallied as much as 4.90% to hit an intraday high of Rs 657.70 during Wednesday's trading session after the company announced a Rs 6,414 crore ($686 million) primary capital infusion led by global investment firm Blackstone and its promoters.The proposed fundraise is among the largest primary private equity investments in a listed Indian non-banking financial company (NBFC).In a regulatory filing, IIFL Finance said its board, at a meeting held on November 10, approved the capital raise through a preferential issue.Blackstone Private Equity will invest Rs 5,000 crore ($535 million) through a preferential allotment of compulsorily convertible preference shares (CCPS). These shares will convert into equity shares at Rs 602 apiece, in line with the regulatory pricing, within 18 months of allotment.Meanwhile, the company's promoters, Nirmal Jain and R. Venkataraman, will invest Rs 1,264 crore ($135 million) through a preferential allotment of warrants. Anchorage Capital will also participate in the transaction with a primary equity investment of Rs 150 crore ($16 million).The company and its promoters have entered into definitive agreements with Blackstone and Anchorage Capital for the proposed transaction, which remains subject to customary regulatory and shareholder approvals.According to  IIFL Finance,  the capital infusion will strengthen its capital adequacy, lower its cost of funds and accelerate growth in its gold finance business, a secured retail lending segment.The proceeds will also support IIFL Finance's ambition to emerge as one of India's largest diversified retail NBFCs.The company aims to tap Blackstone's global network and expertise in operations, technology, data and AI to expand its secured lending businesses, attract talent and strengthen its market position.The proposed appointment of Blackstone representatives to the company's board is also expected to enhance governance standards and oversight.Welcoming the investment, founder and Managing Director of IIFL Finance Nirmal Jain said the partnership would provide the company with additional capital to expand its businesses, invest in technology and deepen co-lending partnerships with banks while maintaining a disciplined approach to risk and capital.Also read: Kalyan Jewellers shares surge 10% to hit upper circuit on strong Q2 earningsIIFL Finance share price performance and Technical indicatorsIIFL Finance shares have gained around 11% over the past week. items.summary: IndiGo has extended the suspension of commercial flights to four destinations in Saudi Arabia amid continuing safety and security concerns, with services to Jeddah and Madinah halted until November 21 and those to Riyadh and Dammam suspended until November 30, 2026.The airline announced the extension in a travel advisory on social media platform X on November 10, stating that the decision followed a review of the prevailing security situation."Following a careful assessment of the safety and security considerations, IndiGo has further extended the suspension of flights to and from Jeddah and Madinah until 21 November 2026 (inclusive), and Riyadh and Dammam until 30 November 2026 (inclusive)," the airline announced in its advisory.IndiGo said it was contacting affected passengers through the details provided during booking. Customers are being informed about ticket re-accommodation, refunds and alternative travel arrangements."Timely notifications are being sent to affected customers using the contact details provided at the time of booking. We remain committed to keeping our customers informed and extending the necessary assistance during this period," the airline said.— IndiGo6E (@IndiGo6E) Reiterating its position on passenger and crew safety, the airline added, "The safety and security of our customers and crew remain our highest priority. We continue to closely monitor the situation and will share further updates as necessary."The extension comes amid renewed hostilities between Saudi Arabia and Yemen's Houthi rebels following the breakdown of a 2022 truce that had paused fighting in the country's prolonged civil war. The Houthis have previously targeted Saudi airports, energy infrastructure and military installations.On November 8, Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Energy confirmed that an administrative building belonging to Saudi Aramco in Riyadh had been targeted in an attempted attack.An official source at the ministry said falling shrapnel caused minor damage to the building. No injuries or fatalities were reported."The incident resulted in falling shrapnel that caused minor damage to the building, with no injuries or fatalities reported, thankfully," the source stated.Also read: UAE flight cancellations continue as airlines suspend Saudi routes until November 19"The source added that the relevant authorities promptly responded to the incident and took the necessary measures," the ministry's statement added.The incident followed claims by Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree that the group had conducted six military operations targeting strategic and military installations across Saudi Arabia using ballistic missiles, cruise missiles and drones.Saree claimed that the first operation targeted King Khalid International Airport, oil storage tanks and an Aramco distillation tower in Riyadh."The first operation targeted Khalid International Airport, oil storage tanks, and a distillation tower belonging to Aramco in the Saudi enemy's capital, Riyadh, and, by Allah's grace, successfully achieved its objective," Saree said.He also claimed that subsequent operations targeted Aramco facilities in Khurais, Pumping Station No. 8 in Dawadmi, a National Guard camp in Najran and troop positions east of Al-Jawf Governorate.The airline has not announced any further changes to the suspension dates.

items.title: Hidden pain! Why did investors lose money in 750 smallcaps when Nifty rallied 2500 points?
items.summary: The Nifty has staged a strong recovery over the past month, surging nearly 13% as foreign investors returned to Dalal Street and heavyweight stocks bounced back from their recent lows. Yet, the rally has brought little relief to hundreds of smallcap investors, with more than 750 stocks delivering negative returns during the same period.An analysis of stock market data compiled by ACE Equity shows that 769 stocks declined between October 8 and November 8, even as the benchmark Nifty recovered sharply. The Nifty climbed 2,812 points, or 12.65%, during this period.The contrasting performance highlights the narrow nature of the market recovery, with foreign institutional investors (FIIs) largely favouring established large-cap companies, while smaller stocks continue to struggle. The weakness has been particularly painful for retail investors, many of whom have substantial exposure to midcap and smallcap companies following their strong performance in previous years.Hundreds of stocks remain under pressureSeveral well-known companies feature among the stocks that have declined despite the Nifty's recovery. According to ACE Equity data, eMudhra fell 33.73% between October 8 and November 8, while Wardwizard Innovations & Mobility declined 32.53%.Genesys International lost 31.58%, Morepen Laboratories dropped 30.93%, and KRN Heat Exchanger & Refrigeration fell 30.90%. Sterlite Technologies declined 30.22%, while MTAR Technologies slipped 26.79%. Electronics Mart India lost 24.39%, Kirloskar Oil Engines fell 24.54%, and RR Kabel declined 21.44%.Other notable laggards included Netweb Technologies, down 16.91%, HFCL, down 15.88%, and Praj Industries, which lost 12.29%.Also Read: FIIs are back with a bang but why are stocks from only 2 sectors their favourites? The losses show that the market recovery has left behind a substantial number of companies across technology, pharmaceuticals, engineering, manufacturing and other sectors.For investors holding these stocks, the sharp improvement in benchmark indices has done little to offset the damage suffered during the broader market correction.Why is Nifty rising while smallcaps struggle?Apurva Sheth, Head of Market Perspectives and Research at SAMCO Securities, believes the divergence comes down to buying being concentrated in a handful of heavyweight stocks."A lot of investors are scratching their heads thinking why their portfolio isn't moving up with Nifty. The simple answer is you don't own what is moving up," Sheth said.According to his analysis, the Nifty Top 10 Equal Weight Index gained 10.64% over the preceding month, while the Nifty Midcap 150 and Nifty Smallcap 250 indices each declined 2.74%. The Nifty Microcap 250 fell 5.32%.The first major reason behind the divergence is valuation. Several largecap stocks had suffered heavy losses during the market correction that began in January 2026, bringing their valuations to more attractive levels.This encouraged investors to return to established companies as crude oil prices eased and concerns about the global economic outlook moderated.Smaller companies, meanwhile, entered the correction with relatively elevated valuations following their earlier rallies. Investors have remained selective amid concerns about earnings visibility and the sustainability of growth.Foreign money is chasing large companiesThe second major factor is the return of foreign institutional investors. After months of sustained selling, overseas investors have begun deploying substantial capital into Indian equities, helping lift banking, technology, telecommunications and other heavyweight stocks.Foreign investors have bought more than $4.1 billion worth of Indian equities so far in November, according to Reuters, marking the strongest monthly inflow since September 2024. However, foreign institutions generally prefer large, liquid companies where they can deploy substantial amounts without significantly affecting share prices.This has benefited stocks such as ICICI Bank, HDFC Bank, Infosys, Bharti Airtel and Reliance Industries. According to Sheth, ICICI Bank and Infosys each gained 16% over his one-month review period, while Bharti Airtel advanced 14.61%. Kotak Mahindra Bank rose 10.08%, HDFC Bank gained 10%, and Reliance Industries climbed 8.44%.The ten heavyweight stocks in his analysis delivered an average return of 10.19%, highlighting how concentrated the rebound has been.For smaller companies, the absence of similar institutional buying has limited the recovery despite improving sentiment across the broader market.Can the broader market catch up?The broader market has also faced pressure from stretched valuations, uneven earnings performance and reduced risk appetite following months of geopolitical uncertainty and high crude oil prices.Although the September-quarter earnings season has shown signs of improvement, investors are increasingly distinguishing between companies delivering sustainable profit growth and those whose earlier valuations were driven by aggressive expectations.The next test for Dalal Street will be whether sustained foreign inflows and stronger corporate earnings encourage buying beyond the largest companies.Disclosure: This article was written by Podishetti Akash, who is not a SEBI-registered Research Analyst or an Investment Adviser. Iran crisis fuels a crude war in Myanmar
items.summary: Myaing, Myanmar: Myanmar's small-scale oil prospectors are under fire from all sides as rebels and the military battle to capture a cottage industry increasingly lucrative amidst the Middle East energy shock."As long as we work here, bad luck can kill us," said Htun Aung, a worker on an artisanal oil well in Myanmar's arid heartlands.Also read | Jensen Huang case: Nvidia CEO love affair scandal revives push for tougher US line on China"But if the reality of death is hard to face, then making a living is even harder," said the 52-year-old, speaking under a pseudonym for security reasons.Myanmar imports 90 percent of its fuel oil, official figures show, making it particularly vulnerable to supply issues caused by the US-Israeli war on Iran.But the central region of Magway hosts a hardscrabble industry of domestic prospectors manning grimy derricks that squelch up crude oil in humble quantities.The area is dubbed "Anyar Dubai", associating the Anyar landscape with the oil boom Emirate, despite the pitiable $50 per week earned by workers like Htun Aung who spend their days drenched in foul crude run-off.With prices at Myanmar's petrol pumps nearly double what they were in late February, the underground "black gold" is an increasingly coveted prize of war.Also read | Trump's Iran war may be 'militarily' over, but economic siege still haunts"We just want to live in peace," said Htun Aung. "But now they strike from one side and the others strike from the other -- they keep attacking each other.""We've had to flee three, four, five times already," he added. "We run here, we run there. We fill up our motorbikes with fuel and run again."Digging inAllied pro-democracy rebels claim to have controlled oil fields in Magway's Myaing township since 2023, the third year of a nationwide civil war triggered by a coup.They patrol the dusty territory in a westward crook of the Irrawaddy river in ragtag columns and outfitted with rocket-propelled grenades, flak jackets, tote bags and flip-flops.Air and drone strikes in Myaing so far this year have already exceeded 2025's total, according to ACLED, a monitor that estimates more than 100,000 people have died since the putsch.Rebels shelter in foxholes, camouflaged among thousands of oil wells dug in an unregulated practice dating back centuries.Engine winches chug day and night, plunging plumbing tubes dozens of metres down boreholes before dragging them up filled with crude oil slurry.Prospectors pay landowners up to $3,500 to lease a spot to drill,one veteran said, with no guarantee they will hit oil.Some wells yield dribbles while others gush profit, filling tarpaulin-lined pits and barrels with oil hauled off to improvised refineries for processing into petrol and diesel."Anyar Dubai" has been "going viral" for its plentiful supply, said rebel spokesman Pyae Phyo Kyaw, at a time when Myanmar military-held areas have been rationing petrol.He touted recent offensives fending off military advances, but admitted being battered by counter-attacks."We see it primarily as an attempt to destroy what has been a strong supply route and source of revenue for us," said the 35-year-old, speaking under his real name.Myanmar's military could not be reached for comment.But in September, a month-long military operation claimed to have captured over 130 wells in Myaing and 735 more in neighbouring Pakokku township.Black marketScores of pro-democracy factions and ethnic minority armed groups are fighting the military over the 2021 coup that ousted the elected government of Aung San Suu Kyi.As the war grinds on, all sides battle to fill war chests with the tax or trade of natural resources: gem mines, rare earth mineral deposits, gold or teak.Oil projects are not generally contested.The major ones are under staunch military guard, and on-the-books output is tiny by international standards -- around 6,000 barrels a day last year, according to the US Energy Information Administration.But artisanal fields are coveted by rebels precisely because of their modest size, according to Thomas Kean, senior Myanmar consultant for the International Crisis Group."Part of the reason why they're significant is because they're not globally significant," he said, explaining that they are small enough to thrive under the radar, yet big enough to fund guerrillas.Spiking oil prices may not directly drive conflict, said Kean, highlighting a broader military campaign to evict rebels from heartland footholds by squeezing revenue sources.But as the spoils of war become more profitable, the stakes get higher."We're talking about millions of barrels a year coming out of these oil fields," he added."With global prices what they are, that's a significant amount of money."

Fed’s Christopher Waller opens door to 50-basis-point December rate hike after hot CPI
items.summary: Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller's remarks intensified the debate over a possible half-percentage-point interest-rate increase in December after US inflation data came in hotter than expected on Tuesday, Bloomberg reported.In a speech delivered in London before the release of October’s Consumer Price Index, Waller said he was inclined to support a rate increase in December. He warned that a 50-basis-point move might be necessary if inflation continued to accelerate, arguing that the Fed’s credibility could otherwise be at risk.Hours later, data showed that consumer prices rose more than expected. Core inflation, which excludes food and energy, increased 0.3% from the previous month, meeting the threshold Waller identified as grounds for considering a larger rate increase.Also read: Traders raise odds of 50 bps Fed rate hike as CPI rise exceeds expectationsWaller’s remarks represent the clearest signal yet from a Fed official that policymakers may need to raise rates in December by more than the quarter-percentage-point move markets had expected.Several senior Fed officials, including Vice Chair Philip Jefferson and New York Fed President John Williams, are scheduled to speak this week.Fed watchers said Waller’s comments did not make a 50-basis-point move certain but would add urgency to the debate over how aggressively policymakers must act to contain inflation.“This is not a print that screams out the need to go 50, but certainly provides ammunition to the argument to do so,” Christopher Hodge, chief US economist at Natixis, told Bloomberg.For live updates on US Markets, click hereTom Porcelli, chief economist at Wells Fargo, said he expected the Fed’s policy-setting committee to support another rate increase unanimously, although the size of the move remained open for debate.“This locks it down,” Porcelli said, referring to the likelihood of at least a 25-basis-point increase. “With Waller introducing that idea, the market is going to run with it in the face of this firm print.”Following Waller’s remarks and the inflation report, investors priced in a more aggressive path for interest rates in the coming months. However, markets remained unconvinced that policymakers would deliver a half-point increase in December.Federal funds futures continued to indicate a quarter-point move in December, followed by additional increases of the same size in January and possibly April. Investors had previously expected rate increases in December and March.Waller described the US economy as strong and the labour market as stable but said inflation remained too high.“If, as I expect, the monthly rate of inflation improves in October, I am leaning toward supporting an increase in our policy rate of 25 basis points,” Waller said.“But if the October CPI inflation data out later today are similar to the past two monthly readings—with core CPI inflation around 0.3% or even higher—then a stronger policy move may be needed,” he added. “In that case, I believe a 50 basis point hike in the policy rate should be considered at the December meeting.”Under such a scenario, Waller said a conventional quarter-point increase would do little to reassure the public that the Fed was serious about controlling inflation.“Hiking only 25 basis points would put our credibility at risk, a risk I am not eager to take,” he said.Also Read: Are days of easy money over? Aswath Damodaran warns of a new mkt realityHot CPI intensifies rate debateData released later by the Bureau of Labor Statistics showed that core consumer prices rose 0.3% in October from the previous month, while the headline CPI increased 0.4%.Fed officials held interest rates steady last month, saying the “accumulation of more information” would help them determine the appropriate policy setting.The 10-2 decision followed a unanimous vote in September to raise the benchmark rate by 25 basis points to a target range of 3.75% to 4%. Several policymakers have since indicated that additional increases may be necessary.Data released last week showed that job growth accelerated in October while the unemployment rate edged lower. Fed officials will receive another employment report and a full set of inflation data before their December meeting.During a question-and-answer session with Bloomberg’s Francine Lacqua after the speech, Waller said the Fed did not want to “slam the economy down.”“It’s not that we’re going to jack up the policy rate 150 basis points or 200 basis points,” he said. “We are looking forward and saying we need to do something; at a minimum, probably take back the three insurance cuts that we put in last year.”Waller added that monetary policy had not been “nearly as restrictive as I thought it was.”(Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies. These do not represent the views of The Economic Times)

items.title: Rupee set for another winning run?
items.summary: The Indian rupee may appreciate further against the US dollar over the next couple of months, supported by easing global headwinds, declining crude oil prices, improving foreign capital inflows and a weakening US dollar, according to economists.Speaking to ANI, former UN adviser and economist Santosh Mehrotra said the domestic currency could strengthen further if the recent easing of global economic and geopolitical pressures continues."Overall, we can expect the Indian rupee to appreciate further over the coming couple of months," Mehrotra said, adding that the outlook would depend on whether global headwinds, which are currently subsiding, remain subdued or ease further.Explaining the factors behind the rupee's recent strengthening, Mehrotra said the Democrats' victory in both chambers of the US Congress had weakened the dollar by reducing the political and fiscal risk premium associated with the currency.He noted that the election outcome could make it more difficult for US President Donald Trump to push through his fiscal and spending agenda, potentially limiting fiscal expansion.Mehrotra also pointed to the possibility of de-escalation in the Middle East, which could reduce geopolitical risks and ease the risk premium in international crude oil prices.He said international crude prices, which were around USD 105 per barrel before the US election results, had declined to approximately USD 96 per barrel.With India importing around 90 per cent of its crude oil requirements, lower international oil prices could reduce the country's import bill and provide support to the domestic currency.Mehrotra also highlighted the return of foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) to Indian equity markets as another factor supporting the rupee.He said foreign investors had purchased approximately USD 1 billion worth of Indian equities in November up to November 5, contributing to dollar inflows into the country.Additionally, he noted that the unwinding of investments in artificial intelligence-related stocks and technology companies in the US and North Asian economies could redirect capital towards other emerging markets, including India.Another supporting factor, according to Mehrotra, was the decline in US Treasury yields.He said US bond yields had eased from around 5.3 per cent to 5.2 per cent on the first day following the election results, as investors anticipated that a Democrat-controlled Congress could constrain Trump's fiscal expansion plans.Lower US Treasury yields could reduce the relative attractiveness of dollar-denominated assets and encourage investors to explore emerging-market bonds offering higher returns.Mehrotra added that Indian government securities had also benefited from improving market conditions, with yields declining by 11 basis points in November.Meanwhile, Devendra Pant, Chief Economist at India Ratings and Research Private Limited, told that declining crude oil prices, a narrowing gap between petroleum product and food prices, and the possibility of lower freight rates could further support the rupee.Pant said freight rates could ease if the announcement of no further US military activity in the Strait of Hormuz and surrounding areas translated into a sustained reduction in regional tensions.He noted that these developments, alongside measures taken by the government and the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) to improve dollar availability, could help stabilise the domestic currency.These measures included the RBI directly providing dollars to oil marketing companies, reducing their need to purchase dollars from the market, along with measures relating to gold.Pant further highlighted that lower crude oil prices could moderate gas prices and ease pressure on the government's fertiliser subsidy bill, a major expenditure component that could otherwise affect fiscal calculations.He added that declining oil prices would also reduce the cost of petroleum imports compared with expectations prevailing a week or 10 days earlier.According to Pant, these developments could result in a lower-than-anticipated current account deficit, while capital inflows, particularly foreign portfolio investments, could improve.Asked about the extent of potential rupee appreciation, Pant said it was difficult to predict a specific level, although the overall outlook remained positive."I will not stick my neck out to give a number. The outlook is, you can say cautious optimism, and the rupee is likely to strengthen further," he said.However, Pant cautioned that any adverse geopolitical developments could reverse the currency's strengthening trend.He said that if the temporary truce or peace in the region holds, the rupee could appreciate further. Even in the event of depreciation, he expected the movement to remain orderly rather than witnessing the sharp declines seen over the past year or year and a half.Pant added that the global economic environment was showing signs of improvement, with headwinds originating in the Middle East gradually easing, a development that could benefit India's economy and international trade.

items.title: India's water journey a model: WB official
items.summary: United Nations: From bringing drinking water to millions of households to cleaning one of its most revered rivers, India's efforts to address its water challenges are increasingly drawing attention beyond its borders, with a senior World Bank official describing the initiatives as a model for developing nations."For the World Bank Group, India is a remarkable success story. It's the water journey that every single developing country is looking at," Saroj Kumar Jha, Global Director for Water at the World Bank Group, said in response to a PTI question during a virtual press briefing ahead of the 2026 United Nations Water Conference.Also Read: 2026 set to rank among four warmest years on record, says WMOThe recognition comes at a time when water security is increasingly becoming a global development priority, with countries grappling with the twin challenges of ensuring equitable access to clean water and protecting existing water resources from pollution and unsustainable use.Co-hosted by the United Arab Emirates and Senegal, the UN Water Conference will be held in Abu Dhabi from December 8 to 10.It will bring together world leaders, policymakers and other stakeholders to explore ways to strengthen international cooperation on water security and sanitation.Also Read: As Delhi gasps for clean air, parliamentary panel skips hearing on air pollutionFor Jha, India's experience offers something beyond ambitious targets and large-scale government programmes, a practical blueprint that other developing nations can adapt to their own circumstances.He highlighted several Indian initiatives, including the Jal Jeevan Mission, Namami Gange and Swachh Bharat Mission.Jha said during his recent visit to New Delhi and meetings with Indian government officials, he had encouraged them to use the international conference as a platform to share its experience and demonstrate how large-scale water management initiatives could be implemented."India has done what other countries are now trying to work on, and India offers the how-to part of the water solution," he said.Among the initiatives that have particularly impressed the World Bank is the Jal Jeevan Mission, which has sought to transform access to drinking water in rural India.Highlighting the scale of the programme, Jha said reaching 800 million people with improved drinking water access in less than seven years is a "remarkable" achievement.He described India's efforts to expand drinking water access in both urban and rural areas as "unprecedented", while pointing out that the programme is now evolving beyond expanding coverage to focus increasingly on sustainability, operations and maintenance.India's sanitation experience, too, has found resonance abroad. Jha cited Nigeria's 'Clean Nigeria' campaign as an initiative influenced by India's Swachh Bharat Mission."What India has done is already spreading to many other countries across the globe, and particularly countries in the South are looking at Jal Jeevan Mission as a good model to replicate with popular participation of people, government-strong leadership, adequate financing at all levels," he said.If access to drinking water and sanitation represents one dimension of India's water transformation, the effort to restore the health of its rivers represents another.Jha described the Namami Gange Programme as "remarkably successful" in reducing pollution in the Ganga and improving the overall health of the river.The World Bank has supported the National Mission for Clean Ganga through various financing instruments.For Jha, river conservation also has a significance that goes well beyond environmental protection."Rivers are not just rivers; they are part of our civilisation, part of the human system. People depend on these rivers for their livelihood," he said.The World Bank official also highlighted India's efforts to improve dam safety, saying the bank's funding had helped strengthen the resilience of nearly 900 dams. The establishment of centres of excellence has further helped build technical expertise and institutional capacity in the sector.India's urban water management initiatives also drew praise, particularly efforts to encourage creditworthy municipalities to tap capital markets and mobilise resources for improving civic water services.Jha acknowledged that India continued to face considerable challenges in water management, but said the progress made at both the central and state levels offered valuable lessons for other countries."We are looking at the entire system of water management in India... What they have done in this field is really remarkable, at the state level and the central government level," he said.India is expected to play an active role in the upcoming UN conference.Stephanie Rambler, Senior Sustainable Development Officer at the UN Department of Economic and Social Affairs, said the country is "very active" in preparations.India is expected to send a large high-level government delegation and organise a side event on 'river cities', focusing on water security and resilience, she said.The conference will feature seven plenary meetings and six interactive dialogues, besides special events aimed at accelerating progress towards Sustainable Development Goal 6, which seeks to ensure access to clean water and sanitation for all.
