Russia, Ukraine first peace talks in 9 mths
items.summary: Abu Dhabi: Russian and Ukrainian officials met in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday for their first US-brokered talks since February, after President Donald Trump suggested last week that a broad deal was possible on ending the war in Ukraine and guaranteeing security in Europe.US envoy Jared Kushner told delegates that recent contacts with both sides had "really identified, narrowed the gaps", and the US side had "some good ideas" on how to bridge their differences. Trump, he said, was committed to achieving peace.Also Read: US-mediated talks on ending Russia-Ukraine war begin in Abu Dhabi"He really has asked us to put extra effort into trying to find a solution that hopefully ends the war but also leaves both sides in a much stronger position" to realise their full potential, Kushner said.But more than 4-1/2 years after Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine, and with Russian forces holding about a fifth of the country, Moscow and Kyiv remain far apart - despite Trump's optimism - on terms for a possible settlement.Ukraine's chief delegate, Rustem Umerov, said in his opening remarks that Kyiv was focused on achieving security guarantees and a lasting peace.Also Read: Trump says Iran war's 'militarily' over, but US 'locked and loaded'Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov underlined Moscow's preference for negotiating a broad European security framework before tackling the specifics of the war."The idea of ​​defining clear parameters for a future security architecture, and only then moving on to resolving the actual Russia-Ukraine conflict, is absolutely reasonable," he told reporters in Moscow.European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen on Monday voiced the opposite view, saying wider security talks should come only after a ceasefire in Ukraine. Lavrov again rejected the notion of a truce, saying the Europeans were trying to buy breathing space for Ukraine.Europeans seek a role in the processThe new American drive for a deal has galvanized European officials into pushing for a place at the table to seek an end to the continent's deadliest conflict since World War Two.Before the start of the main meeting, the Ukrainians met separately with European, NATO and EU representatives and the two American envoys, Kushner and Steve Witkoff.France said there could be no lasting peace in Ukraine without addressing European security, and that this required the involvement of the Europeans.Russia had made clear it did not see a place for Europeans at the meeting with the Ukrainians and Americans.On the eve of the talks, Trump said Washington was seeing a "very strong inclination" towards ending the war, and that both sides were "tired of fighting". After meeting privately with Russian President Vladimir Putin's envoy last week at the White House, Trump predicted that a peace deal could emerge soon.Trump has frequently said an agreement was close, without a deal emerging. However, negotiations have picked up again in recent weeks after months in which Washington's attention was focused on the war in Iran.Publicly, there has been no sign that Putin is willing to drop his insistence that Ukraine surrender the entire eastern region of Donbas before a peace deal can be struck.Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy has refused to hand over land that his forces have died defending.Russian front-line advances have slowed to a virtual halt this year but Moscow has been pounding Ukrainian cities and energy facilities, while Ukraine has stepped up attacks on oil refineries and other infrastructure deep inside Russia.A source in the Russian delegation said Russia believed the main thrust of the talks would be trying to hammer out the key elements of a new post-war security framework for Europe.On the eve of the negotiations, Zelenskiy said Ukraine's leverage in the talks was increasing as a result of its recent battlefield performance, which has included retaking some territory in Donetsk, a coal-mining area of the Donbas."Ukrainian forces are currently genuinely strengthening Ukraine's negotiating position," Zelenskiy said in his nightly video address on Monday. He said Russia was suffering "record losses" - an assertion disputed by Moscow - and urged Washington to convince the Kremlin to end the war.US negotiators believe that Zelenskiy and Putin may be willing to strike a compromise on the vital question of territory, each ceding a little, a US official told Reuters.Under the proposed deal, Ukraine would get an end to the war, security guarantees and a roadmap to accession to the EU.A senior Ukrainian official strongly denied that the government would consider any such concessions. The issue of territory could be discussed only at the leaders' level and only in the context of appropriate security guarantees for Ukraine, the official said.

Nvidia board faces 'honey pot' test
items.summary: Revelations that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had an affair with a businesswoman suspected of being a Chinese spy have forced the chipmaker's board to confront more than ordinary executive misconduct, raising existential questions for the company and concerns about the board's ability to investigate its CEO independently.Among corporate leaders, "There have definitely been affair scandals and sexual-harassment scandals. But honey-pot scandals? No," said Ann Lipton, a University of Colorado law professor who follows boardroom issues.She was using a term for an espionage ploy in which an operative entraps a target by feigning romantic interest. Historical examples include the Profumo Affair in the early 1960s and tend to involve diplomatic or political consequences.Also Read: Jensen Huang's price of secret affair: NVIDIA CEO loses $7.4 billion in 30 minutes, drops 2 spots in top 10 richest listUS President Donald Trump said on Monday the FBI was probing Huang's relationship, a day after Nvidia's board launched an internal investigation "regarding the national security concerns raised in news reports," according to an email Huang sent to Nvidia employees and released by the company.The company's advanced semiconductors are at the heart of a global race for AI superiority. China's Foreign Ministry said the spying claim was "a groundless accusation, slander, and a smear."Nvidia co-founder Huang, 63, has no obvious successor and close ties to Trump. He owns 3.6% of its stock and has dozens of direct reports, suggesting a tight grip on the company.Shares in Nvidia fell Monday as Huang's future came under scrutiny. But the stock later trimmed its decline to close 4% lower as some investors bet that the CEO could survive the crisis.BOARD'S CREDIBILITYUnusually among its peers, Nvidia operates without a board chair among its 11 directors. While the company considers all but Huang independent, three independent directors have served since the 1990s and a fourth, Mark Stevens, for most of that time. Only two have joined the board since 2021.The clubby roster may not be so unusual by the standards of charismatic Silicon Valley company founders like Apple's Steve Jobs, who died in 2011.But the US probe has heightened scrutiny of whether directors who have worked alongside Huang for decades are sufficiently independent to investigate his conduct."If you have a figure like Steve Jobs, I think people on Wall Street as well as in Silicon Valley would say they're entitled to some leeway or deference," said Marc Goldstein, head of US research for proxy adviser Institutional Shareholder Services.Such deference could now raise questions about whether the board provided sufficient oversight of a CEO whose own judgment has come under scrutiny.Nvidia said on Sunday that while its board had no reason to believe that either US national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised, its inquiry would examine ​all available information. The board said it had confidence in the CEO and his leadership team.Goldstein said board members running that investigation should be given the latitude to hire their own legal advisers to bolster their credibility.The company also might consider keeping long-serving directors away from the probe, he added, to avoid legal challenges from shareholders claiming it wasn't sufficiently independent.POLITICAL ECONOMYYale University management professor Jeffrey Sonnenfeld said the company faces additional national-security questions because of the ties between Huang and Trump. Trump, who has praised Huang, said on Monday that he had spoken to the executive and thought he would "be in good shape."Washington has imposed restrictions on exports of advanced AI chips to China since ​2022. Last year the Trump administration allowed Nvidia to resume certain China shipments under arrangements in which the US government receives a cut of the company's China chip sales.The deal makes any suggestion of foreign espionage more sensitive for both executives and US government officials, Sonnenfeld said. "That's why you don't want state capitalism arrangements. You don't want the US government to be so involved in private companies," he said.

Warren Buffett’s 7 golden rules for young investors trying to manage finances
items.summary: Young investors often find it difficult to manage their finances as rising number of responsibilities and expenses take a toll on savings. But billionaire and market veteran Warren Buffett has some advice for them.Buffett took control of a struggling textile company at the age of 35 in 1965 and transformed it into Berkshire Hathaway, now valued at more than $1 trillion, with annual after-tax operating earnings of about $45 billion. Buffett handed over the CEO role to longtime deputy Greg Abel this year, and recently passed on the Chairman role to his son, Howard Buffett.The 96-year-old Warren Buffett, even after retirement, continues to inspire generations to come. Here are pieces of his advice that can help young investors.1) Live below your meansWarren Buffett once famously treated fellow billionaire and Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates not at a fancy restaurant, but at his favourite McDonald’s, and that too using coupons. This famously simple act speaks volumes about the market veteran’s frugal lifestyle.He lives in the Omaha house he bought for $31,500 in 1958. The five-bedroom home is now worth about $1.3 million, but Buffett says he would never trade it because it holds memories of raising his three children. He also avoids splurging on expensive cars. The legendary investor drives a 2014 Cadillac XTS, complete with hail damage, because, in his words, giving up half a day to shop for a new car isn’t worth it. He even once had a license plate that read “THRIFTY,” a fitting symbol for one of the world’s richest individuals who chooses to live simply.Also read | Warren Buffett’s 6 golden rules for investors after retirement“I do not think that standard of living equates with cost of living beyond a certain point,” Buffett said at a Berkshire Hathaway shareholders meeting in 2014. “My life would not be happier: it would be worse if I had six or eight houses or a whole bunch of different things I could have. It just doesn’t correlate.” Whether it’s mansions or sports cars, Buffett avoids major purchases that reflect his wealth, believing they may ultimately detract from his happiness.2) Pay off high-interest debt as soon as possibleWarren Buffett also strongly advised people to pay off any high-interest debt they may have, like credit card debt. In fact, the ace investor believes that paying off your credit card debt is one of the best guaranteed ways to get a return on your money.If you are drowning in debt, work out a payment plan to pay back your creditors as soon as possible, or the interest will keep piling up. After you're debt-free, make it a point to set aside funds for investments from your income regularly.3) Think long-term while investingThe legendary investor advocated for long-term investing and not short-term quick trades. Buffett has famously said, "Our favourite holding period is forever." His long-term holdings have included Coca-Cola, American Express and Wells Fargo.By emphasising low costs, diversification, and long-term growth, Buffett’s rule continues to gain attention as a reliable strategy for everyday Americans seeking financial security.Also read | Michael Burry's top 10 life lessons for GenZ: 'Buy half the house you can afford'4) Invest in what you knowWarren Buffett has repeatedly stressed the importance of staying within one's "circle of competence." "You only have to be able to evaluate companies within your circle of competence. The size of that circle is not very important; knowing its boundaries, however, is vital."Buffett famously avoided technology stocks during the dot-com boom of the late 1990s because he believed forecasting the long-term survival of young technology companies was outside his expertise.5) Always have a cash reserveWhile Warren Buffett is a bullish stock market investor, he did encourage people to hold some amount of cash reserves. “You do need oxygen, and if you are ever without it for four or five minutes, you will learn. And cash is that way. So you always need to have it available, because you do not know what will happen,” Buffett told CNBC during an interview earlier this year. He, however, added that while holding cash at certain levels is necessary, it is not a good asset.The legendary investor likes to keep some level of cash to pay obligations and as “dry powder” for any attractive acquisitions.Also read | Peter Lynch on stock picking: 'You shouldn't own a stock if you can't…'6) The 90/10 investment ruleIn his 2013 letter to Berkshire Hathaway shareholders, Warren Buffett introduced his 90/10 investment rule by sharing what he wrote in part of his will. With reference to a cash inheritance going to his wife, he advised his will's trustee to keep 90% of the cash inheritance in an S&P 500 index fund and 10% in short-term government bonds. Buffett believed this mix offers the best balance of growth and stability for non-professional investors. The S&P 500 provides exposure to America’s largest and most profitable companies, while Treasury bonds act as a cushion during market downturns.7) Remember that money isn’t everythingBuffett is among the richest people in the world, but he does not use this metric as a measure of success. “Being given unconditional love is the greatest benefit you can ever get,” he told MBA students in a 2008 talk.“The incredible thing about love is that you can’t get rid of it. If you try to give it away, you end up with twice as much, but if you try to hold onto it, it disappears. It is an extraordinary situation, where the people who just absolutely push it out, get it back tenfold.”Disclaimer: This article has been written by Debaroti Adhikary, who is not a SEBI-registered Research Analyst or an Investment Adviser. items.title: Is AI selloff a window to buy? Morgan Stanley sees multiple buying opportunities on Wall Street
items.summary: As the frenzy around artificial intelligence (AI) fizzles out, Morgan Stanley has struck a positive note, with the international brokerage firm seeing buying opportunities among AI enablers, infrastructure providers and adopters.After Democratic victories in the US midterm elections triggered concerns that a Democrat-controlled Congress would curb excessive AI spending on data centres, tech stocks plunged and have been trading on a seesaw since then. Morgan Stanley noted that Wall Street had undergone an earthquake event over the past week, with significant uncertainty surrounding the impact of the midterms on the data centre build-out, the trajectory of the cycle and the implications for global stocks.It broadly views the recent market weakness as unwarranted. “We see the market moves as an overreaction and think the ultimate impact will be a push-out of some projects from 2028 to 2029, rather than a derailing of the capex story. This has the potential to elongate the AI capex cycle, which has positives including a smoother supply-demand rebalancing across the data centre supply chain, improved credit outlook, and higher lease rates for compute,” it said.Also read | Anthropic retracts details of $69 billion IPO filing sent to bankers. Why analysts are raising worries over valuationsMorgan Stanley has sized the impact on the data centre build-out and flagged implications for stocks, policy and equity strategy across the US, Asia and Europe. "We are recommending a selective ‘Buy the Drop’ strategy and remain most constructive on the hyperscalers, select semis/infrastructure/time-to-power solutions that have de-rated materially, and software enablers and AI adopters as AI value creation broadens,” it further said.How Trump's midterm defeat can impact the AI tradeThe newly elected Democratic governors are unlikely to disrupt projects under construction, leaving 2027 projects unchanged, Morgan Stanley said. However, it believes some 2028 projects in Texas and Ohio will be delayed to 2029, as governors work with legislators to put in place new requirements for data centre developers.The international research firm shifted 5 GW of US data centre capacity from 2028 to 2029, representing 20% of US projects and 10% of global projects. This implies that US data centre capacity additions will decline 4% year-on-year in 2028 and rise 38% year-on-year in 2029. Globally, this implies data centre additions will rise 9% year-on-year in 2028 and 20% in 2029.“This could create an air-pocket across the tech supply chain in 2028, leading to a reduction in pricing power or a build of inventory, although we believe valuations are pricing this in across many names, with the key risk being the sustainability of margins. We also believe this creates an attractive opportunity to potentially build data centres abroad and forecast 20GW of potential spillover across Asia and EMEA,” it added.That said, Morgan Stanley is mindful that delays in project approvals or initiation, on top of existing constraints around labour and materials, could put downward pressure on its 2028 capex estimates and prolong the build-out and capex cycle.“We are highly focused on increased (exponential) compute efficiencies from leading labs in 2027 to allow products to scale with less compute. Compute constraints aren't new, and they may just stay around longer with further data centre delays,” it added.Finally, financing remains available, but the midterms should deepen the quality divide, Morgan Stanley said. With capex forecasts unchanged, it still expects higher AI-related debt issuance in 2027, led by hyperscalers. New construction financings and neoclouds face greater scrutiny, making tenant quality, a credible path to energisation and contractual protections increasingly important.“We see more limited exposure to new restrictions for projects already backing outstanding bonds, although execution risk remains. Slower competing development should support stabilised, cash-flowing assets, reinforcing our preference for colocation over hyperscaler data-centre ABS.”Also read | Nithin Kamath says speculative craziness brought more people into US markets: ‘Nothing expands markets like greed, FOMO’Which AI stocks to buy?Given the significant price weakness across a range of AI-related stocks following the US election results, Morgan Stanley provided its updated views on which stocks or sectors look most attractive, highlighting three key areas. It has three main buckets of investment recommendations.These include hyperscalers (Amazon, Meta, Google and Microsoft), select data centre supply chain names, and software enablers or AI adopters. Nvidia is also mentioned among the stocks, but it belongs to the semiconductor category rather than the hyperscaler category. The brokerage also suggested a ‘Buy the Drop’ approach, identifying selective ways to play the AI investment opportunity post-midterms.Disclaimer: This article has been written by Debaroti Adhikary, who is not a SEBI-registered Research Analyst or an Investment Adviser. items.title: China's trade surplus tops $1 trn for 2nd straight year, exports jump 35%
items.summary:
China's trade surplus exceeded USD 1 trillion for a second straight year, according to official data released Tuesday, as pressure mounts for greater balance in trade with Beijing.
Exports in October surged 35.2 per cent from a year earlier, the customs agency said. Exports have grown rapidly this year supported by high-tech goods like semiconductors and autos. Imports rose 41.6 per cent year-on-year.
Between January and October, China logged a USD 1.04 trillion trade surplus, even as the trade surplus narrowed last month to USD 105.3 billion from USD 133.5bn in September as imports picked up pace.
That puts China on track for surpassing last year's record USD 1.2 trillion trade surplus.
"We expect Chinese exports to stay strong for the rest of this year, led by electronics and autos," said Dave Chia, an economist at Moody's Analytics.

items.title: Ozempic, Wegovy to carry new FDA warning over rare risk of vision loss
items.summary:
Popular weight loss drugs including Ozempic and Wegovy will carry a new warning about a possible rare side effect that can sometimes lead to permanent vision loss, US health regulators announced Monday.
The Food and Drug Administration said the risk will be added to the labeling of all GLP-1 drugs, the blockbuster medications used to treat obesity, diabetes and several other medical conditions. The class includes a dozen injectable or pill-based drugs, including widely used brands like Zepbound and Mounjaro.
The eye condition, known as non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy, can cause significant vision loss. The problem, which has been reported with all GLP-1 drugs, is caused by decreased blood flow to the optic nerve, although the underlying cause isn't understood, the FDA said.
FDA scientists began looking into the problem after the publication of a 2024 medical paper tying the condition to certain patients taking semaglutide, the active drug in Eli Lilly's Ozempic.

items.title: US Senate advances bill to fast-track data centre, energy project permits
items.summary:
The Senate on Monday advanced bipartisan legislation aimed at speeding up permitting reviews for data centres and other infrastructure projects, in the first major action since last week's election that soundly repudiated President Donald Trump and congressional Republicans.
The Senate voted 73-25 to formally take up the bill, which senators and the president have pushed as a way to meet growing demand for electricity and other forms of energy that now face yearslong delays in getting to the grid.
The legislation's sweeping changes would shorten the timeline to get big energy projects started - both for clean energy and fossil fuel projects - and make sure data centres pay for the energy they use. Anger over artificial intelligence data centres and rising electricity helped usher in a wave of Democrats pledging to clamp down on the massive, energy-hungry structures.

"Iran militarily is effectively over," Trump said. "We're just keeping it the status quo."

The fire at the HABAS plant in Aliaga, Izmir province, also injured 13 people, two of them critically, President Recep Tayyip Erdogan said in a televised address following a scheduled Cabinet meeting.
"Judicial and administrative investigations have been launched into the explosion," Erdogan said. "The reasons and circumstances of this tragic event, which has deeply saddened our nation, as well as whose negligence was involved and who is responsible, will be revealed."
Provincial Governor Suleyman Elban said that a crane fell into a furnace as it was replacing a boiler, causing an explosion in a nearby steel mill. There were 200 workers in the vicinity instead of the usual 300 because production had been halted for the boiler switch, he said.

items.summary:
British author M John Harrison was named the winner of the 2026 Booker Prize for his dystopian satire 'The End of Everything' at a ceremony here on Monday night.
Aged 81, Harrison becomes the oldest author to win the prestigious literary prize after a writing career spanning 60 years.
Just 198 pages, 'The End of Everything' was also the shortest novel on this year's shortlist and won because judges felt it is a book that "leaves you with a twinge of optimism" about the world.
"I feel like a proper writer at last, totally lacking in confidence," said Harrison.
"Prizes like this one, not that there are any prizes quite like the Booker, are so important in a landscape of industrialised fiction," he said.
Fiction authors from the UK dominated the shortlist of the 2026 Booker, including Scottish American past winner Douglas Stuart - shortlisted this year for 'John of John'.

items.title: US stocks: Dow rockets 1,100 points, S&P over 2% as oil slide cools inflation worries; Nvidia slumps
items.summary: US stocks rallied sharply on Monday as falling oil prices eased inflation concerns and helped the S&P 500 rebound from its steepest weekly decline since April 2025. Technology shares also surged, even as AI heavyweight Nvidia tumbled amid uncertainty surrounding CEO Jensen Huang, Reuters reported.The S&P 500 climbed 172.97 points, or 2.34%, to close at 7,549.83. The Nasdaq Composite gained 671.13 points, or 2.73%, to 25,250.55, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average surged 1,104.20 points, or 2.16%, to 52,394.36.Stocks fell sharply last week after Democrats swept the US midterm elections, fuelling concerns that tighter regulations could threaten the durability of the artificial intelligence trade.Nine of the 11 major S&P 500 sectors gained more than 1% on Monday. Industrials and consumer discretionary led the advance, rising about 4% each.The broader market rallied despite a steep decline in Nvidia, the world’s second-most valuable company. Its shares touched their lowest intraday level since March 31 as investors questioned Huang’s future at the chipmaker following an internal investigation into whether he had been targeted by a foreign intelligence operation.“The AI story is not going away if people are worried about that. The Democrats are not going to destroy AI. They can’t. It’s got a life of its own. They can put regulation around it, but they’re certainly not stopping it,” Ken Polcari, partner and chief market strategist at SlateStone Wealth in Jupiter, Florida told Reuters.A sharp decline in crude-oil prices provided further support by easing concerns about inflation after US President Donald Trump played down the likelihood of renewed strikes on Iran.“Oil prices for sure, if they’re down, that’s certainly adding fuel to the fire,” Polcari said.Investors are now awaiting key inflation reports. The Labor Department is scheduled to release October’s Consumer Price Index on Tuesday, followed by the Producer Price Index on Friday.Some Wall Street analysts described last week’s sell-off as an overreaction. Morgan Stanley and UBS said the rout in AI-linked stocks appeared excessive, arguing that the risk of severe restrictions on data-centre development remained low despite Democratic majorities in Congress.Expectations for an interest-rate increase at the Federal Reserve’s December meeting remained above 80%, according to CME FedWatch. October’s strong jobs report was seen as giving the central bank room to continue raising rates, even as oil prices eased.Richmond Fed President Tom Barkin said on Monday that the central bank should adjust monetary policy “with care” as it formulates its response to inflation.Chipmakers rallied strongly. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index jumped about 7% after tumbling more than 12% last week, its steepest weekly decline since the week ended April 4, 2025.Nvidia was the index’s only decliner on Monday, while Broadcom and Advanced Micro Devices provided the biggest boosts.KKR shares advanced after the investment firm reported record quarterly profit. Constellation Energy, which has exposure to the AI infrastructure buildout, surged more than 10% after its adjusted third-quarter profit exceeded expectations.Berkshire Hathaway’s Class A shares also gained after the conglomerate reported lower third-quarter profit.(Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies. These do not represent the views of The Economic Times)

items.title: Americans growing more worried about jobs amid rising prices, finds NY Fed survey
items.summary: Americans grew increasingly concerned about the US labour market in October, with expectations of a higher unemployment rate over the next year reaching their highest level since April 2020, according to a survey released by the Federal Reserve Bank of New York on Monday.The New York Fed's October Survey of Consumer Expectations showed that households anticipated a greater likelihood of involuntary job losses, although the perceived risk remained relatively low. However, respondents also expressed greater confidence in their chances of finding employment after losing a job.For live updates on US Markets, click hereThe growing pessimism over employment came alongside expectations that inflation would remain elevated. Consumers projected inflation at 3.9% over the next year, 3.3% over three years and 3% over five years, unchanged from September. All three readings remain above the Federal Reserve's 2% inflation target.Expectations for commodity prices were mixed, with households anticipating a more moderate rise in gasoline prices over the next year compared with their September projections.The survey's findings contrasted with official employment data released on Friday, which showed the US economy added 165,000 jobs in October, while the unemployment rate edged down to 4.1%. The report also included significant upward revisions to recent hiring figures.Also Read: Fed’s Barkin urges rate policy caution, Goolsbee warns of inflation concerns as AI risks loomMeanwhile, households reported a modest improvement in their current financial situations, while expectations for their finances over the next year remained unchanged. Perceptions of access to credit, both currently and in the future, were also steady.The survey was conducted throughout October, ahead of the US midterm elections, which resulted in broad-based Democratic gains, including control of both houses of Congress.

items.title: 5 reasons why Wall Street added $1.5T today
items.summary: US stock market today, 9 November, 2026: Wall Street has added $1.5 trillion in market value, but the biggest surprise is where investors are putting their money. Semiconductor stocks are recovering, Tesla is climbing and oil prices are falling. The Dow Jones has gained more than 1,000 points, while the S&P 500 is up 2.17% and just 4% away from a record high. Yet Nvidia is falling nearly 5%.Monday's US stock market rally: Here's 5 reasons why Dow Jones, S&P 500 and Nasdaq are rallying today1. AMD stock jumps 12% as investors return to semiconductor stocksAdvanced Micro Devices (AMD) is leading the semiconductor recovery. Its shares jumped more than 11% during Monday's trading and later extended gains to more than 12%, according to the latest November 9 update.The rally has two important drivers. First, investors are buying chip stocks after last week's heavy sell-off. Second, Oppenheimer upgraded AMD to Outperform from Market Perform and set a $600 price target.The company's growing AI business and its Google Cloud partnership are also supporting investor interest. AMD's rebound is particularly important because chipmakers were among the biggest losers during last week's technology sell-off.2. Tesla stock rises 5.45% as Magnificent Seven stocks recoverTesla (TSLA) shares climbed 5.45% to $377.74 in the November 9 market snapshot. The recovery reflects renewed buying across major technology companies after weeks of losses.Meta Platforms also gained around 5%, while Apple (AAPL) rose 2.16% to $349.77. Alphabet, Amazon and Microsoft advanced more than 2%.These companies have significant weight in major US stock indexes. Their gains are helping the Nasdaq and S&P 500 recover. Tesla's rise also suggests investors are looking beyond semiconductor stocks for opportunities in the technology sector.3. Nvidia stock falls nearly 5% as Jensen Huang investigation unsettles investorsNvidia (NVDA) is moving in the opposite direction. Its shares fell 4.98% to $177.34 in the supplied midday snapshot, despite the broader technology rally.The pressure follows reports concerning CEO Jensen Huang and Alice Huang, a Singapore-based business executive reportedly suspected of gathering information for China. Jensen Huang acknowledged an extramarital relationship and said he would cooperate with the investigation.Nvidia's board has launched an independent investigation. The company has said it has no reason to believe that national security or its business secrets were compromised.4. Broadcom and Marvell stocks jump more than 8% as AI chip demand returnsBroadcom (AVGO) and Marvell Technology (MRVL) each gained more than 8% on Monday. Intel (INTC) and Micron Technology (MU) also moved higher.The iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) climbed more than 6%, showing that the recovery extends across the chip industry.Investors are returning to semiconductor companies after last week's selling raised questions about AI investment, data centre construction and future chip demand.However, the recovery does not mean those concerns have disappeared. Investors will continue watching technology companies' capital spending plans and demand for AI infrastructure.5. Constellation Energy and Barrick Mining stocks gain as earnings support Wall StreetConstellation Energy (CEG) shares climbed around 8%, while Barrick Mining (B) advanced approximately 4% following their quarterly results.Constellation is attracting attention because of its role in supplying electricity to data centres. Rising demand for computing power has made electricity availability an important part of the AI investment story.Barrick's gains also show that Monday's buying is not limited to technology companies. Investors are finding opportunities in other sectors as market sentiment improves.Why are oil prices falling while gold rises?Crude oil is another important part of Monday's market movement. WTI crude futures fell around 3.2% to $87.90 per barrel, while Brent declined approximately 4%.Investors are watching developments in the Iran war and the possibility that tensions could ease. Lower oil prices can reduce fuel costs for businesses and ease some inflation concerns.Gold moved in the opposite direction, rising 1.5% to around $4,140 an ounce. Bitcoin traded near $75,000 after retreating from weekend levels above $76,000. The 10-year US Treasury yield also moved higher to approximately 4.89% from Friday's 4.87%.Can the S&P 500 reach a new record high?Monday's rally comes after a difficult four weeks for Wall Street. The S&P 500 lost 5.6% over that period, while the Nasdaq Composite declined 10.2%. Both indexes recorded four consecutive weekly losses, their longest losing streaks since March.The S&P 500 and Nasdaq had reached record highs on October 6. The S&P 500 is now around 4% below its previous peak.

items.title: Nvidia CEO's secret affair has a hidden angle
items.summary: The allegations on Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang being targeted by a Chinese intelligence operation have brought a critical US national security concern into focus: whether access to one of America's most influential technology executives could have been used to gather sensitive information on its AI capabilities, semiconductor supply chains and strategy to maintain its lead over China.US intelligence agencies reportedly believe that Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman and former executive at Singapore-based data centre company Megaspeed, was gathering information for Beijing after developing a close relationship with Jensen Huang. The Financial Times, citing people familiar with the matter, reported that the US intelligence community believed she had been recruited by China's Ministry of State Security.Also read: I was unfaithful to my wife: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admits secret affair with Chinese spy Alice HuangWhile the allegations have not been independently established publicly, the potential national security implications are significant. Nvidia is a leading supplier of the advanced processors used to train and run AI models, and its technology has become central to America's efforts to maintain an advantage over China in artificial intelligence.The company's board has initiated an independent investigation, saying it has no reason to believe that US national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised. However, the episode has prompted lawmakers to seek answers about the company's safeguards against foreign intelligence operations.Why is Nvidia so important to America's AI and military ambitions?Nvidia's importance extends beyond its position as one of the world's largest semiconductor companies. Its graphics processing units (GPUs) are used to train and operate advanced AI models, making them a critical part of the computing infrastructure underpinning the AI industry.The technology also has potential military and intelligence applications, including in autonomous systems, surveillance, cyber operations and other advanced defence capabilities.This is why access to advanced AI processors has become a strategic issue in the US-China rivalry. Washington has maintained restrictions on exports of its most advanced AI chips to China since 2022, citing concerns that the technology could accelerate Beijing's military modernisation.The stakes were highlighted in January, when former White House national security adviser Matt Pottinger told a congressional hearing that allowing Nvidia's H200 processors to be sold to China could strengthen Beijing's capabilities in areas ranging from nuclear weapons and cyber warfare to autonomous drones and intelligence operations, according to Reuters.The controversy involving Huang therefore raises a broader question: could access to the leadership of a company at the centre of America's AI infrastructure provide a foreign intelligence agency with information valuable to its technological and strategic ambitions?Also read: China dismisses 'Chinese spy' narrative in Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang probe; calls it 'unsubstantiated'Could China have gained access to sensitive US technology or business information?One of the central concerns surrounding the reported intelligence operation is the possibility that proximity to Nvidia's CEO could have provided access to information about the company's technology, business strategy, customers and future product plans.The New York Times reported that US intelligence agencies believed Alice Huang's relationship with Jensen Huang could have provided her with insights into Trump's thinking on artificial intelligence.Nvidia has maintained that its cloud customers in Asia receive ordinary business information, not sensitive trade secrets or information related to US national security.Its board has also said it has no reason to believe that company secrets or national security were compromised.Also read: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's secret affair: Why did US intelligence suspect Alice Huang of spying for China?Could the alleged operation have implications for US semiconductor export policy?Another important dimension is the potential access to information about Washington's semiconductor export restrictions and the discussions surrounding them.The US has sought to limit China's access to advanced AI processors, arguing that the technology could strengthen its military and intelligence capabilities.Nvidia, meanwhile, has a commercial interest in maintaining access to the Chinese market and has sought permission to sell certain advanced processors there.The Financial Times reported that US national security officials had privately expressed frustration with Huang over his efforts to persuade Trump to allow Nvidia to export its H200 chips to Chinese customers.The New York Times also reported that the relationship between Huang and Alice Huang could have provided her with insights into Trump's thinking on AI.This has raised questions about whether an intelligence operation targeting a senior technology executive could potentially provide information about US policy discussions, export restrictions and the positions of influential decision-makers.Megaspeed's involvement may raise supply chain concernsThe connection to Megaspeed adds another layer to the national security concerns.The Singapore-based data centre company buys equipment powered by Nvidia chips and rents computing capacity to businesses, including Chinese technology companies.According to The New York Times report, Megaspeed had bought more than $4.8 billion worth of Nvidia chips over the past two years. The company has also come under US scrutiny over allegations that its network may have helped Chinese businesses access advanced AI processors restricted from export to China.The concern for Washington is that overseas data centres and intermediaries could potentially provide Chinese companies with access to computing resources powered by restricted American technology.The Financial Times also stated that a sister company in Malaysia bought at least $4.8 billion of advanced AI equipment containing Nvidia technology between June 2024 and February 2026.In a Reuters column, Robyn Mak on Monday noted that Chinese technology companies have legally accessed processors restricted in mainland China through overseas data centres operated by neocloud providers such as Megaspeed. Mak also pointed to US investigations into suspected illegal chip-smuggling operations through Southeast Asia.The allegations therefore bring two national security concerns into focus: the possibility of foreign intelligence gathering around a major US technology company and the challenge of preventing restricted semiconductor technology from reaching Chinese customers through overseas supply chains.Could the controversy prompt tighter US export controls?The allegations could increase pressure on Washington to strengthen oversight of Nvidia's sales channels and the movement of advanced AI processors through third countries. US authorities have already been examining whether overseas companies and data centres are being used to circumvent restrictions on semiconductor exports to China.The controversy could intensify scrutiny of customer verification, the end-use of advanced chips and the role of intermediaries in the global AI computing supply chain.The issue is particularly sensitive as the Trump administration has been weighing how to balance US chipmakers' commercial interests against concerns about China's access to advanced AI technology.In December, Trump announced that the US would allow Nvidia to export its H200 processors to China under conditions that included a 25% fee for the US government. Regulations subsequently introduced requirements for third-party testing, customer security procedures and restrictions on the volume of chips that could be exported.The decision had already drawn criticism from China hawks in Washington, who argued that such sales could strengthen Beijing's military capabilities.Mak argued that the fallout could ultimately hurt China's AI ambitions more than it helps if Washington comes under pressure to tighten enforcement and close existing workarounds.Why are US lawmakers seeking answers from Huang?The national security implications have prompted congressional scrutiny.Three Republican committee chairmen — Brian Mast of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, John Moolenaar of the China Select Committee and Eric Crawford of the Intelligence Committee — have asked Huang to appear for a closed-door briefing on November 18.In their November 4 letter, the lawmakers sought answers about his reported interactions with Alice Huang and Nvidia's security protocols against foreign adversary espionage.They said the allegations raised significant national security concerns about China's access to sensitive US technology and information.Separately, Democratic Senator Chris Coons has pledged to investigate the reported links between the Trump administration, Chinese intelligence and major AI industry executives, according to the Financial Times.The congressional inquiry could examine not just the reported relationship but also the extent to which Nvidia's customer interactions, information-sharing practices and security procedures protect sensitive American technology.What is at stake for the US-China AI race?The controversy comes as Washington and Beijing compete for leadership in artificial intelligence, an area often viewed as strategically important for economic competitiveness, military capabilities and technological influence.The US has sought to retain its advantage through restrictions on advanced semiconductor exports, while China has been working to develop domestic alternatives and secure access to computing resources.Nvidia occupies a particularly important position in this competition because its processors power a substantial part of the global AI infrastructure.Reuters columnist Mak noted that heightened scrutiny could accelerate the shift among Chinese companies towards domestic alternatives, including chips developed by Huawei and smaller competitors. However, the columnist also argued that tighter US restrictions could make it harder for Chinese technology companies to access advanced computing resources through overseas data centres.The controversy thus has implications beyond Nvidia. Any tightening of export controls or greater restrictions on overseas access to American AI processors could affect the pace at which Chinese companies develop and deploy advanced AI systems.Nvidia's board has initiated an independent investigation, overseen by independent directors and external legal counsel, where Huang has agreed to cooperate with the inquiry. The board has said it has no reason to believe that US national security or Nvidia's trade secrets were compromised.The US intelligence assessment concerning Alice Huang has not been publicly substantiated through disclosed evidence. China has rejected the espionage allegations as groundless speculation.The investigation and the congressional scrutiny will therefore be important in establishing whether any sensitive information was accessed, what information may have been sought and whether Nvidia's security protocols need to be strengthened.For Washington, the larger issue is how to protect the technology, expertise and supply chains underpinning its AI advantage at a time when competition with China is increasingly becoming a national security priority.

items.summary:
The Reserve Bank of India's net short position of USD 239 billion in the forward market is likely to limit the rupee's appreciation despite a recovery in foreign portfolio investor (FPI) inflows, according to a report.
The Reserve Bank of India's (RBI) forward book stood at a net dollar short position of USD 239 billion as of September 2026, reflecting its commitment to provide dollars when buy-sell swaps mature. This will require the central bank to accumulate dollars as capital inflows improve, limiting the rupee's appreciation, IDFC First Bank Economic Research report said.
Around USD 40 billion of the short position matures within a year, USD 56 billion in one to three years and the remaining USD 143 billion in three to five years. The longer-duration positions are largely linked to the FCNR (B) scheme, it added.

items.title: Parliament's Monsoon session unprorogued for 88 days, breaks 2008 record
items.summary:
Parliament's Monsoon session has remained unprorogued for 88 days since both Houses were adjourned indefinitely on August 13, breaking the previous record of 87 days in 2008.
As of Monday morning, neither the Lok Sabha nor the Rajya Sabha had been formally prorogued, keeping open the possibility of convening an extended sitting of the existing session.
The government's decision not to prorogue (formally end) the Monsoon session has kept alive speculation about the possibility of convening Parliament at short notice to consider the proposed constitutional amendment linked to the implementation of the Women's Reservation Bill, which seeks to increase the strength of the Lok Sabha from 543 seats to a maximum of 850 through delimitation.
An extended or special sitting of Parliament within the same session requires a minimum notice of two days, whereas convening a fresh session requires at least 14 days' notice.

Nasdaq-listed travel booking platform MakeMyTrip's India subsidiary has received Sebi's approval to launch an initial public offering (IPO), according to an update available on the markets regulator's website on Monday.
MakeMyTrip (India) Ltd (MMT India) had filed draft papers with Sebi in July through the confidential route. After examining the draft documents, the regulator issued its final observations on November 6.
Sebi's observations mark an important step in the IPO process, allowing the company to proceed with preparations for its public issues, subject to applicable regulatory requirements.
The proposed IPO is expected to comprise a sale of equity shares in MMT India by its parent MakeMyTrip and its wholly-owned subsidiary, ibibo Group Holdings (Singapore) Pte Ltd, the Gurugram-headquartered company said in a regulatory filing with Nasdaq.

India's exports of oilmeals, mainly used as animal feed, fell 28.51 per cent in the April-August period of the current fiscal year to 12.82 lakh tonne, as a slump in soybean meal sales weighed on shipments, an industry body said on Monday.
Exports were 17.93 lakh tonnes in the same period a year earlier, the Solvent Extractors' Association of India (SEA) said. Total oilmeal exports in the 2025-26 fiscal year stood at 37.68 lakh tonnes.
Soybean meal exports plunged 73 per cent to 2,05,000 tonnes from 7,57,000 tonnes a year earlier.
"Indian soybean meal has faced severe pricing pressure in international markets during August 2026, trading around USD 622 per tonne compared to global benchmarks near USD 445 per tonne," the SEA said in a statement.
Cheaper supplies from South American producers such as Argentina and Brazil continue to capture major market share, it added.

items.summary: Global banks are turning more bullish on Indian stocks as the market’s sharpest rally in more than four years draws record foreign inflows.HSBC Holdings Plc lifted local equities to overweight from neutral, citing resilient earnings and more reasonable valuations. Citigroup Inc. raised its 12-month target for the NSE Nifty 50 Index by nearly 8% to 28,000, pointing to improving profit growth and lower oil prices.The calls suggest that Indian equities’ recent rebound may have further to run. The views signal a broader reset in sentiment toward India after a prolonged stretch of underperformance, as investors seek markets less vulnerable to concerns over stretched AI valuations.“India offers diversification and low volatility in Asian markets dominated by AI stocks,” HSBC strategists including Herald van der Linde wrote in a note. They favor banks, industrials, consumer discretionary companies, insurers and hospitals.135673874The benchmark index is up nearly 8% this month, the most since July 2022, making India one of the best-performing major markets globally. Local stocks slipped Monday, bucking a rebound in Asian peers, as investors booked profit following the recent rally.Overseas funds bought a net $3.6 billion of local shares in the four days through Thursday, putting them on course for their biggest-ever weekly inflow. Provisional data showed another $1.5 billion of purchases Friday.The shift marks a sharp reversal after foreign investors spent much of the past two years cutting exposure to India as they chased AI-driven gains elsewhere in Asia and the US. That left positioning relatively light.Citi sees significant scope for foreign positioning to rebuild. A percentage-point increase in active fund allocations to India could generate about $12 billion of inflows, according to analysts including Surendra Goyal and Vijit Jain, after AI “crowded out almost everything else”.The brokerage expects Nifty earnings to grow about 15%-16% annually for fiscal years 2026-2028. It also sees cheaper crude supporting the economy and corporate profits, estimating a $10 decline in oil prices could boost Nifty earnings per share by about 2%.

Indian sector of Southern Ocean sees rising oxygen levels, finds study
items.summary:
Dissolved oxygen levels in the Indian sector of the Southern Ocean (ISSO) have significantly risen over the past three decades, even as oceans elsewhere are showing the trend of declining oxygen levels, a study by scientists at a Goa-based institute has found.
The scientists attributed the oxygenation primarily to enhanced ocean ventilation - the process through which surface waters are mixed and transported into the ocean interior, replenishing oxygen at greater depths.
Oxygenation in the ISSO intensified between 1993 and 2025, particularly in the Polar and Antarctic zones, as per the study conducted by researchers from the National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR), Goa.
The findings stand in contrast to the broader trend of declining oxygen levels in oceans worldwide, which scientists have linked to global warming, increased ocean stratification and weakening circulation.

items.title: All about Nvidia CEO Huang's affair controversy
items.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang acknowledged having an extramarital relationship with a business executive suspected by US intelligence of gathering information for Beijing, as the chipmaker's board launched an independent investigation into reports that its founder was targeted by a foreign intelligence operation. While Huang has apologised to his family and company employees saying he was ‘unfaithful’ to his wife, Nvidia said it has no reason to believe that US national security or the company's secrets were compromised.US President Donald Trump has defended Huang, describing him as an "honourable guy" who has done an "amazing job" for the country. Trump also expects Huang to remain at the helm of Nvidia, adding that the executive deserved to have his side of the story heard.Also read: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's secret affair: Why did US intelligence suspect Alice Huang of spying for China?The controversy follows reports by The New York Times and the Financial Times that US intelligence agencies had identified a close relationship between the Nvidia leader and Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman associated with Singapore-based data centre company Megaspeed. US intelligence officials reportedly believe she was gathering information for Beijing.Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang issues key statementIn a draft email to Nvidia employees, Huang acknowledged having an extramarital relationship, "I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did.”In a separate message reported by The New York Times, he apologised to his family and company employees, taking responsibility for his actions. "I take full responsibility for what I did and the hurt I caused, and I accept the criticism that comes with it," he wrote.Addressing Nvidia employees, Huang also acknowledged that he had fallen short of his responsibilities towards them. “My responsibility is to serve you and be worthy of your trust. I have fallen short of that responsibility. I am fully committed to Nvidia and will work to earn back your confidence," he said.He also requested privacy for his family, saying they bore no responsibility for his choices.Huang has not directly addressed the allegations that the business executive, aka, the Chinese spy was gathering information for the country. He has, however, supported Nvidia's investigation and committed to cooperate with it.Also read: Nvidia opens probe into CEO Jensen Huang over affair with woman suspected of spying for ChinaNvidia announces independent investigationNvidia's board of directors announced an independent investigation following reports that Huang had been the target of a foreign intelligence effort. The investigation will be overseen by a committee of independent directors, assisted by external independent legal counsel.In its statement, Nvidia said, "While the Board has no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised, the Board's inquiry will examine all available information." The company added that the board prioritised US national and economic security, which it said was paramount to Nvidia and its shareholders.The board also expressed confidence in Huang and his leadership team and said it would provide further updates as appropriate.Huang, 63, will continue as Nvidia CEO during the investigation, it clarified.Speaking on Huang meeting thousands of customer executives every year, the company previously said that it regularly receives updates from the US government regarding parties and entities of concern and acts accordingly.Trump defends Nvidia CEOTrump has publicly defended Huang amid the controversy, describing him as an honourable person and praising his contribution to the US."I have not spoken to him about it. I just know he's a fine person, but you never know what is going on," Trump told reporters. "I think he's an honourable guy," he said, adding that Huang had "done an amazing job for our country".When asked whether Huang should remain Nvidia's CEO, Trump replied: "I think so. Sure."Trump also suggested that Huang should be given an opportunity to explain himself. Asked whether he would take Huang on his planned trip to Asia, Trump said, "I don't know, but I'd certainly take him."The remarks came amid reports that Trump had been briefed on intelligence findings concerning Huang's relationship with the Chinese businesswoman roughly a year ago but had chosen not to act on the information, according to The New York Times.The Financial Times separately reported that a US government memo based on intelligence information about the alleged relationship had been shared with a small group of senior US officials shortly before Trump travelled to Beijing for a summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping.The FT also reported that Trump had held multiple meetings with Huang since beginning his second presidential term in 2025. Huang had personally lobbied Trump earlier this year to allow Nvidia to export its H200 chips to customers in China.Who is Alice Huang, the Chinese spy?Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, is a Chinese national and former senior executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based data centre company.According to The New York Times, Alice Huang was previously a television reporter in China before becoming a senior executive at Megaspeed. The company buys equipment powered by Nvidia chips and rents computing capacity to businesses, including Chinese technology company Alibaba.US intelligence agencies reportedly concluded that Alice Huang had developed a close relationship with Jensen Huang and was passing information directly to Beijing.The Financial Times reported that the US intelligence community believed she had been recruited by China's Ministry of State Security, the country's main intelligence agency.Jensen Huang had previously described their association as a normal business relationship.Megaspeed and its connection to the Nvidia caseMegaspeed has come under US scrutiny over concerns that Nvidia's advanced AI chips may have been diverted to China.The New York Times reported that Megaspeed had been examined for potentially steering Nvidia AI chips to China. According to the publication, the firm bought more than $4.8 billion worth of Nvidia chips over the past two years.The Financial Times reported that Megaspeed was spun off from a Chinese gaming company in 2023. US authorities have been investigating companies, particularly in Southeast Asia, suspected of helping China obtain advanced chips in violation of US export restrictions.Nvidia had previously launched an internal investigation into allegations concerning the diversion of chips through Megaspeed but assessed that there was no evidence of wrongdoing, according to the Financial Times.US lawmakers step up actionSenior Republican lawmakers in the US House of Representatives earlier asked Huang to brief Congress about the allegations and Nvidia's security protocols.In a letter dated November 4, Brian Mast, chairman of the House Foreign Affairs Committee; John Moolenaar, who leads the China Select Committee; and Eric Crawford, chairman of the Intelligence Committee, sought a closed-door briefing from Huang on November 18.The lawmakers sought answers about the New York Times report and Nvidia's security protocols against foreign adversary espionage. The letter said the allegations raised significant national security concerns regarding China's access to sensitive US technology and information.The lawmakers added that Congress needed to determine the extent to which US national security had been placed at risk.Meanwhile, Chris Coons, a Delaware Democrat who is due to chair the Senate Foreign Relations Committee from January, pledged to open an investigation."Congress will investigate and get answers," Coons wrote on X, referring to what he described as the relationship between the Trump administration, Chinese spies and AI billionaires.Political and corporate reactions to Jensen Huang affairUS Secretary of State Marco Rubio declined to comment on the allegations when asked about the report, describing it as an "internal corporate matter", according to AFP.Technology analyst Dan Ives of investment bank Yorkville Ives described the investigation as a "black eye moment" for Huang. Ives said the controversy could trigger multiple congressional inquiries and create an overhang on Nvidia's stock.He also warned that the development could increase scrutiny of the company's chip sales to China, which remains a key issue in Washington.Huang's position at Nvidia could also come under scrutiny depending on the outcome of the board's investigation, Ives said, adding that the CEO's importance to the company's global strategy made the controversy a risk for the stock.Separately, Elon Musk responded to a social media post about the controversy. The post suggested that while Huang had done something incredibly foolish, there might have been no malicious intention. Musk replied, "I agree."Nvidia stock downNvidia shares came under pressure in out-of-hours trading following the announcement of the board investigation.Perpetual futures trading on the Hyperliquid exchange and after-hours shares trading on the Blue Ocean system showed Nvidia shares at around $180.30 on Monday, down approximately 3.4% from Friday's Nasdaq closing price of $186.64.The development has raised concerns about the potential impact of the controversy on investor sentiment, particularly given Huang's importance to Nvidia's business and its global AI strategy.South Korean govt intervenes in Nvidia CEO caseSouth Korea stated that Nvidia's contracted GPU deliveries to the country are expected to proceed without disruption despite the controversy surrounding Huang.Vice Science Minister Ryu Jemyung told a parliamentary budget committee on Monday that 10,000 GPUs funded under a 2025 supplementary budget had already arrived and were in use. GPUs planned for 2026 were under contract and expected to enter service this year."We expect production and the delivery schedule for contracted volumes to proceed without disruption," Ryu said, adding that the ministry was monitoring developments and discussing prices and schedules with Nvidia Korea.Meanwhile, a planned visit to South Korea by Huang's daughter Madison Huang, an Nvidia senior director, was cancelled.South Korean AI startup Rebellions said her planned visit to its headquarters and a dinner with partners had been called off due to unavoidable internal circumstances at Nvidia.Kakao Mobility also cancelled a photo session and question-and-answer event with her. However, the company said its business agreement with Nvidia would proceed, with senior director Gaurav Agarwal attending instead.Nvidia AI Day Seoul, a two-day event expected to attract around 2,000 participants to discuss physical AI, agentic AI and infrastructure, was proceeding as planned, according to South Korean media.The investigation's findings, the response from US lawmakers and any further developments concerning Megaspeed's business dealings with China will be key to determining the wider implications for Nvidia.

items.summary: Shares of Mamaearth parent Honasa rallied as much as 5% to their day’s low of Rs 494 on the BSE on Monday after the company reported a strong set of earnings for the second quarter of FY27. The company reported an 86.7% year-on-year (YoY) rise in consolidated net profit to Rs 73.25 crore for the September quarter on Friday, November 6, supported by strong demand across its beauty and personal care brands, wider distribution and improving profitability.Revenue from operations increased 35.9% to Rs 731.19 crore from Rs 538.06 crore a year earlier, marking the company's highest quarterly revenue growth since its stock market listing in November 2023.Red More: Samvat 2083 outlook: 8 triggers that could turn Sensex, Nifty correction into a rally by next DiwaliVarun Alagh, chairman, CEO and co-founder of Honasa Consumer, said the September quarter reflected the company's efforts to build a larger presence in the sector. "We delivered our highest growth since listing, with revenue growing 36% YoY and EBITDA nearly doubling to Rs 93 crore," Alagh said.Why is Jefferies bullish?Jefferies has raised its target price on Honasa Consumer to Rs 700 from its previous level, indicating an upside potential of 45%, while maintaining its 'Buy' rating.The brokerage said the company delivered its strongest growth since listing, supported by broad-based momentum across brands and sales channels. The strong performance also translated into a significant margin beat, with both EBITDA and net profit doubling year-on-year. Mamaearth recorded high-teen growth, while The Derma Co (TDC) and newer brands continued to scale up rapidly. Expanding distribution is also providing greater visibility into the growth potential of newer brands.Despite elevated input cost inflation, gross margin contracted by only around 55 basis points year-on-year. EBITDA margin expanded by more than 3.8 percentage points to 12.7%, comfortably exceeding expectations.Jefferies attributed the improvement to operating leverage, a better channel mix and greater advertising and promotion (A&P) efficiency in core brands. Overall A&P spending increased 36% year-on-year, broadly in line with revenue growth, with a significantly higher allocation towards newer brands. Lower sales commissions following the shift towards offline channels and quick commerce also supported operational efficiency.Read More: Finolex Cables shares fall 5% after rallying 20% during Muhurat Trading session. More upside ahead?Jefferies remains confident that Honasa can sustain its current margin trajectory of 12.5% in the second half of the financial year. The company has also retained its guidance of 100-150 basis points of annual margin expansion over the next five years, targeting a 15% margin by FY30.Innovation and renovation will remain key focus areas as the company continues to develop products for younger consumers. Honasa is also planning to expand its presence in the hair colour category through another brand, with an announcement expected soon.Taking into account the stronger performance, Jefferies has raised its earnings estimates by 10-16%.Honasa Q2 highlightsHonasa continued to expand its offline retail network during the quarter, particularly across general trade outlets such as neighbourhood stores. Its general trade distribution network reached approximately 3.2 lakh outlets, supported by efforts to increase product availability across markets.The company also reported more than 40% YoY growth in offtake through modern trade channels, which include supermarkets and organised retail chains. items.title: Chandra and Mehli reconnect at Tata HQ
items.summary: Mumbai: Fresh from Italy, where Tata Motors announced the acquisition of commercial vehicle maker Iveco, Tata Sons chairman N Chandrasekaran invited Mehli Mistry, the late Ratan Tata's confidant and a trustee of the Tata Education and Development Trust, to Bombay House on Thursday.Coming just days after the two were seen together at the wedding celebrations of Mehli's daughter Laila, the meeting reinforced a belief within Tata circles that relations between the two are improving after more than a year marked by a broader power shift within the Tata Group following the death of Ratan Tata.Also read: Plea seeking Tata Sons listing filed in Bombay High CourtPeople familiar with the matter said Chandrasekaran and Mehli, who was voted out of the two principal trusts that hold majority in Tata Sons by Noel Tata and others, discussed issues that had affected their ties.Mehli-Chandra meet focused onrebuilding trust, restoring equationMehli's challenge against his removal is pending before the Maharashtra Charity Commissioner (MCC).Mehli and Chandrasekaran's conversation last week was focused on rebuilding trust and restoring a working equation. Mehli later left for Dubai, with both sides appearing keen to move beyond a difficult period in one of Tata Group's most significant internal relationships.For much of the past decade, Mehli and Chandrasekaran were regarded as allies. After the dramatic ouster of Cyrus Mistry as chairman of Tata Sons in 2016, Mehli played a key role in the legal fight that followed between Cyrus and Ratan Tata. When Ratan Tata had to choose a successor, he picked Chandrasekaran, assisted by Mehli. Mehli later backed Chandrasekaran's second and third terms as chairman of Tata Sons. The third term, however, became contentious after Noel Tata, who succeeded Ratan Tata as chairman of Tata Trusts, opposed Chandrasekaran's reappointment.Mehli and Chandrasekaran's relationship survived differences in personality and style. Those who know Mehli describe him as intensely loyal, fiercely independent and refreshingly blunt. Friends admire his willingness to say in a room what others prefer to whisper outside it. Critics point to a temperament that can run ahead of diplomacy. The redeeming feature, according to people who have worked closely with him, is that his anger rarely lingers.Also read: Noel Tata proposes splitting Tata Sons as alternative to RBI-mandated listingChandrasekaran is a different kind of leader. Publicly measured and understated, he has cultivated the image of a consensus-builder since arriving at Bombay House. Yet colleagues say beneath that calm exterior lies a highly competitive executive with sharp political instincts and an acute understanding of institutional power.Then came the post-Ratan Tata era. Ratan Tata's death in Oct 2024 altered the balance of influence within Tata Trusts. Disagreements that had previously been settled privately soon surfaced within the trusts.Mehli and fellow Tata Trusts trustees Darius Khambata, Pramit Jhaveri and Jehangir Jehangir argued that information on Tata Sons covered under Article 121 of the company's Articles of Association had not been shared with them, limiting their ability to take informed decisions. The four trustees voted Vijay Singh off the Tata Sons board.Concerns about the emerging situation prompted a visit to Delhi by Noel, Tata Trusts vice-chairman Venu Srinivasan, Khambata and Chandrasekaran, who briefed senior government officials on governance issues within the trusts.Mehli, who was inducted into Sir Dorabji Tata Trust (SDTT) and Sir Ratan Tata Trust (SRTT) by Ratan Tata and remained one of his most trusted advisers, increasingly found himself at odds with the emerging power structure. He was eventually voted out of the two trusts by Noel, Srinivasan and Singh, who is also a vice-chairman of the trusts.Among the relationships most affected was Mehli's equation with Chandrasekaran. Differences emerged over how developments within the trusts were characterised and communicated to external stakeholders, with Mehli maintaining that his interventions were driven by governance concerns. Communication between the two subsequently became infrequent.People said Chandrasekaran later made efforts, through intermediaries and directly, to reopen channels of communication with Mehli. Mehli remained a respected figure among trustees, a prominent voice within the Parsi community and an influential presence in discussions concerning the Tata legacy.Mehli has challenged the end of his trusteeship before the Maharashtra Charity Commissioner (MCC), where the matter is pending. He, however, never withdrew his support for Chandrasekaran's stewardship of Tata Sons. In filings before the MCC, he said he had backed Chandrasekaran's reappointment for a third five-year term and was a signatory to the resolution approving it.Chandrasekaran's second term as chairman ends in Feb 2027. His third term is linked to his continuation as a director of Tata Sons, which requires the trusts' approval at the company's annual general meeting (AGM). However, Tata Sons was unable to hold its AGM on Aug 18 after it failed to secure the requisite quorum. The impasse followed restrictions imposed by the MCC on SRTT, preventing it from joining SDTT in nominating a joint representative for quorum purposes.

items.title: Gland Pharma shares jump 4% as Q2 profit jumps 58%, revenue rises 23% YoY
items.summary: Shares of Gland Pharma gained 3.89% to Rs 3,254.60 during Monday's trading session after the pharmaceutical company reported a strong performance for the September 2026 quarter, with revenue rising 23% year-on-year (YoY) and net profit surging 58%.The stock also touched a fresh 52-week high of Rs 3,345 during the session.Gland Pharma reported a 23% YoY increase in its Q2 revenue from operations to Rs 1,834 crore, from Rs 1,487 in the corresponding quarter of the previous year. Net profit for the September 2026 quarter rose 58% YoY to Rs 290.8 crore, compared with Rs 183.7 crore in the same quarter last year.The company's adjusted EBITDA increased 50% year-on-year, while the adjusted EBITDA margin stood at 27%. Its profit after tax (PAT) margin also expanded by approximately 350 basis points during the quarter.Business segment performanceGland Pharma's CDMO business contributed 45% to overall revenue and recorded 31% year-on-year growth in Q2 FY27. Meanwhile, its Critical Injectables business accounted for the remaining 55% of revenue, registering growth of 18% during the quarter.The company continued to invest in research and development, with total R&D expenditure reaching Rs 107.7 crore in Q2 FY27, equivalent to 6% of consolidated revenue. This was higher than Rs 81.7 crore reported in the year-ago quarter. The expenditure was primarily directed towards complex product development and increasing the number of regulatory filings.During the September quarter, Gland Pharma launched four molecules in the US market: Sugammadex, Erythromycin, Fluorouracil and Atropine Sulfate.The company also filed 11 Abbreviated New Drug Applications (ANDAs) and received 10 approvals during Q2 FY27. With these additions, its cumulative US ANDA filings reached 399, of which 350 had been approved and 49 were awaiting approval.Management commentaryCommenting on the quarterly performance, Srinivas Sadu, Executive Chairman of Gland Pharma, said the company delivered another quarter of strong growth, supported by improved execution across its businesses. He highlighted the 31% growth in the CDMO segment, driven by expanding customer engagements, strategic partnerships and a strong opportunity pipeline.He also noted that continued investments in manufacturing capabilities, innovation and capacity expansion would help the company capitalise on increasing global outsourcing opportunities and create long-term shareholder value.Gland Pharma share price Gland Pharma shares have gained approximately 30% over the past three months. Its PM2.5 concentration is 298 µg/m³, while PM10 stands at 358 µg/m³.Pune AQI stands at 412Pune has recorded an AQI of 412, with hazardous air quality. The PM2.5 concentration is 271 µg/m³ and PM10 is 328 µg/m³.Noida reports AQI of 373Noida's AQI stands at 373, with air quality classified as hazardous. The city has recorded PM2.5 levels of 261 µg/m³ and PM10 levels of 358 µg/m³.Rajkot records AQI of 358Rajkot has reported an AQI of 358, also falling in the hazardous category. Its PM2.5 concentration stands at 238 µg/m³, while PM10 is recorded at 284 µg/m³.Chennai AQI reaches 188Chennai has recorded an AQI of 188, with air quality classified as unhealthy by AQI.in. The PM2.5 concentration stands at 109 µg/m³ and PM10 at 132 µg/m³.Ahmedabad reports AQI of 179Ahmedabad's AQI stands at 179, with air quality classified as unhealthy. Its PM2.5 level is 95 µg/m³, while PM10 is recorded at 114 µg/m³.Mumbai records AQI of 156Mumbai has reported an AQI of 156, with air quality in the unhealthy category. The city's PM2.5 concentration stands at 67 µg/m³ and PM10 at 81 µg/m³.Dehradun AQI stands at 155Dehradun has recorded an AQI of 155, with air quality classified as unhealthy.
