items.title: Crude cools, but war risks keeps mkts guessing
items.summary: New Delhi: Oil prices may remain elevated as President Donald Trump's weakened political position after the midterms complicates efforts to end the Iran war and Tehran grows more emboldened, industry executives said, although crude oil cooled hours after the results came out.Brent futures dropped $9.27, or 8.9%, to $94.29 a barrel, touching the lowest level since September 4. US West Texas Intermediate crude futures were down $7.44, or 7.8%, to $88.54.Also read: And quiet flows the Don: Trump goes from rage to rapproachementTrump could seek to demonstrate strength by intensifying military operations against Iran, but Democrats' control of Congress could constrain his ability to fund the war in West Asia. "Trump has already lost the midterms and cannot seek re-election. To prove the American public that he is right, he may escalate the military conflict," an executive said.Since the war began, Trump has pursued two objectives: intensifying military pressure on Iran while keeping oil prices in check, often by signalling that the conflict was nearing an end and would not escalate. With the elections behind him, he may be more willing to let oil prices rise in the short term and focus on achieving his military objectives.A decisive outcome, whether through military action or a deal, would be preferable to the prolonged stalemate that has imposed heavy costs on oil importers, executives said. But an escalation involving ground forces could also prolong the conflict, further disrupting energy supplies and raising costs for consumers.A deal with Iran could offer Trump a way to claim victory while bringing down oil prices and easing the cost-of-living pressures that contributed to the Republicans' defeat. However, a settlement that allows Iran to impose a permanent toll on shipping through Hormuz could undermine Trump's ambition to be remembered as one of America's greatest presidents, another executive said.Also read: Trump admits Iran war hurt Republicans in midterms but says ‘Iran thing’ had to be doneIndian refiners would ideally prefer unrestricted passage through Hormuz, an executive said.Whether or not Iran is allowed to levy a toll, a resolution that restores the flow of oil through the strait would reduce the risk premium on crude prices and bring down freight rates, lowering procurement costs for importers such as India, he said.Brent crude is near $100 a barrel, while freight and insurance costs are several times higher than before the war. Brent was around $70 before the war started.The cost of the prolonged disruption has been compounded by uncertainty over the reliability of supplies. Although oil flows through the strait have risen sharply in the past two months, they remain expensive and unpredictable, making the current situation unsustainable for importers."This is better than no flows at all but definitely not sustainable," an executive said.

items.title: Don Trump goes from rage to rapproachement
items.summary: TOI Correspondent From Washington: The man who posts on social media at the drop of a hat, at all times and at odd hours, sometimes a dozen posts an hour, was rendered rather speechless after an electoral thrashing for the ages.Now a lame-duck President for all purposes but still armed with enormous executive powers, Donald Trump reacted to the Republican rout first with a mix of denial and defiance, and later with nonchalance and some conciliation. His initial reaction when the Democratic demolistion came into view early on Tuesday night was one of denial. “I wasn’t on the Ballot and if I was, we would have won IN A LANDSLIDE!” he posted on his propaganda platform “Truth Social.”Track US Senate Elections Result 2026 Live Updates hereThen it was a couple of rage posts about Fox News -- his favored propaganda network whose coverage became funereal as the night wore on -- and blaming Republican candidates, including defeated Texas Governor Greg Abbott, a wheelchair-bound GOP stalwart who was thwarted in his bid for a third term.“If Greg Abbott hadn’t become a RINO (Republican in Name Only) in the last six months of his Political Life, he wouldn’t have lost. He went back to his original formula, and it wasn’t pretty!” he wrote, throwing the veteran under the bus and absolving himself of all blame. He told Fox News that some voters simply “didn’t like the candidates.”Shortly after midnight, he posted a photo of a red baseball cap with the word VETO on it – suggesting that he will simply block any Democrat-written bills, creating a deadlock since Dems do not have the 2/3rds majority in both chambers to override a presidential veto.Then he went silent for more than nine hours, but not before he also told a C-Span in a live phone call that he would work with Democrats and not veto everything they sent, even though he has the right to do so.Also read: US midterm elections 2026: Democrats sweep House and Senate, deal Trump major blow"We're going to work with the Democrats, to make sure things go well for our country... We have a lot of friends in the Democratic Party,” he said in a conciliatory tone at odds with his familiar combativeness.Democrats too have every reason to work with the President. The U.S Constitution (Article I, Section 7) requires a two-thirds majority vote in both the House of Representatives (290/435) and the Senate (67/100) to overcome the veto – although the qualifier is 2/3rds majority of those “present and voting." Dems are well short of that double which last occurred in 1965 during the Lyndon Johnson Presidency.But a testing time is afoot even within the Republican ranks. The rout shocked and angered many conservatives, some of whom began to turn on Trump publicly. “Dems look like they might get 56 (Senate seats).. Rs will never get that back for a long time. You ignore primaries for years, anoint a charlatan as not just leader but God, and then mimic his retardation every day for a decade, at some point the chickens come home to roost,” raged Daniel Horowitz, a commentator at the right leaning outlet The Blaze. "It's on him. It's not on anybody else. It's a total, complete rejection of President Trump," Bill Miller, a top Republican lobbyist in Texas, told BBC, calling it “a disaster of the first magnitude” that nobody saw coming.Also read: US Vice President JD Vance says Iran war is 'the reason we lost' midterms 2026Actually, every poll and survey other than MAGA affiliated ones saw it coming, although the scale was not foreseen by most. In fact, Democrats went to polling day wary of the “too good to be true” projections given past setbacks, particularly in 2016 when Trump himself did not appear to believe he would win. This time around, he tried to conjure up victory in the face of imminent defeat with bravado and bluster, but voters had other ideas. They trussed him up by giving Democrats a comfortable majority in both chambers of Congress.

items.title: Correction? AI stocks tumble post midterms
items.summary: US stock market update: Dow Jones rallies today after Democrats win Congress - Democrats have won both the Senate and the House, and the stock market liked it. By 10:44 am ET on Wednesday, the Dow Jones was up 1,245 points, or 2.40%, at 53,032. The S&P 500 rose 1.52% and the Nasdaq gained 1.82%. But not every stock joined in. Data centre companies, Tesla and SpaceX fell. Democrats made gains in Texas and Georgia, where public opposition to new data centres is growing, and investors fear tighter rules could slow the AI boom.Democrat Gina Hinojosa defeated Governor Greg Abbott after promising an immediate pause on new data centre projects until lawmakers introduce stronger safeguards. The result added to pressure on AI infrastructure stocks, with CoreWeave falling 7%.The concern is significant because Texas accounts for an estimated 27% of planned US data centre capacity, according to Wells Fargo.Will a Democratic Congress slow the AI boom? Why data center stocks fell as the Dow gained 1,100 points The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 2.13% to 52,889.71, gaining 1,102.99 points. The S&P 500 climbed 1.49% to 7,681.76, while the Nasdaq Composite advanced 1.97% to 25,871.41.ALSO READ: US stock market stages big rally today: Why is Dow Jones surging? Dow jumps 1,100 points as S&P 500 and Nasdaq turn green, with healthcare stocks at the centreWith Republicans losing control of both chambers of Congress, President Donald Trump's administration could face greater difficulty passing major policy changes.Investors also saw the election outcome as a way to reduce uncertainty. Markets had been watching closely for the results because changes in Congress could affect tariffs, government spending, energy policy and regulations.Scott Chornert, head of US equity strategy at Citi Research, described the election as a clearing event, suggesting that investors could now move beyond the uncertainty surrounding the vote.Amazon was among the strongest performers in the technology sector. Its shares gained around 7.1%, while Alphabet rose 3.4% and Meta Platforms added 1.6%.Other major technology stocks also moved higher. Apple and Microsoft gained nearly 6% in morning trading, according to market reports.McDonald's also climbed around 3.9% after reporting quarterly profits above market expectations. Amgen gained about 3% following its results.Block shares jumped 15% after the payments company raised its full-year gross profit outlook.Tesla and SpaceX sharesElon Musk's companies moved in the opposite direction. SpaceX shares fell around 1.9% to $138.91 in the supplied market data, while Tesla declined nearly 4% in morning trading.Musk had spent heavily backing Republican candidates during the election campaign. The Democratic victories could bring greater scrutiny of some of his business interests, particularly government contracts, artificial intelligence and the proposed merger between Tesla and SpaceX.AI and data centre stocks face fresh pressureThe election results also brought attention to the future of the US artificial intelligence industry.Democrats made gains in states such as Texas and Georgia, where local opposition to the rapid expansion of data centres has been growing.Data centres require large amounts of electricity, land and water. Their expansion has raised concerns about power costs, local infrastructure and the impact on nearby communities.Investors are now considering whether tighter rules could delay new projects and affect companies supplying equipment and computing services.Shares of data centre operators, including IREN, Hut 8, Applied Digital and Core Scientific, fell between 1.2% and 13%.Nvidia shares slipped 0.41% in the supplied market snapshot, while AMD gained around 4.8% after issuing a stronger growth outlook for 2027.Solar stocks rise while defence shares fallClean energy companies were among the biggest beneficiaries of the election outcome.The Invesco Solar ETF jumped 8.3% as investors considered the possibility that federal support for solar and other clean energy projects would remain in place.Defence stocks moved lower. Northrop Grumman and Lockheed Martin each lost more than 4% in morning trading.The change followed concerns that a Democratic-controlled Congress could make it harder for Trump to secure approval for his proposed $1.5 trillion defence budget.Palantir also fell around 1% amid concerns about its exposure to government and defence contracts.Oil falls while gold and cryptocurrencies move higherWTI crude oil fell 2.31% to $93.87 a barrel, while Brent crude declined 2.27% to $101.25. Investors were watching developments surrounding the US-Israeli war on Iran and its possible impact on oil supplies and inflation.Gold futures rose 2.53% to $4,040.10 an ounce. Silver gained 4.40% to $51.94.Cryptocurrencies also moved higher. Bitcoin rose 3.69% to $80,500.84, while Ether gained 6.68% to $2,433.23. XRP advanced 3.01% to $1.32.The US 10-year Treasury yield also moved lower, falling to 4.93% from 4.97% in the previous session.

items.title: Aswath Damodaran trims his Anthropic IPO valuation to $1.45 trillion; Dean of valuation explains why
items.summary: Valuation expert Aswath Damodaran trimmed his valuation estimate for AI giant Anthropic to $1.45 trillion, from his earlier estimate of $1.475 trillion which was already lower than the industry estimates of $2 trillion.The 'Dean of Valuation' in a long blogpost said his earlier valuation estimate which was lower than the overall market view received strong reactions. Some of them were solely based on emotion, he said, as they held strong conviction in the company. Some of it was based on cost of capital, which the analyst believes reflects a fundamental disconnect with market history, current market pricing and basic business sense.Also read | Dean of valuation Aswath Damodaran pegs Anthropic's worth at $1.475 trillion ahead of mega IPOHis latest $1.45 trillion valuation accounts for the trailing 12-month revenue and operating income numbers to include the just-leaked third quarter numbers. “The equity value that I obtain for Anthropic is close to the lower end of the offering price estimates, but as I noted at the time that I posted it, and will reinforce again now, it is a function of not just my upbeat story about the company, but also one about how the AI products and services market will evolve over time,” he wrote.Aswath Damodaran’s worries for AnthropicDamodaran estimates Anthropic’s target revenues will reach a trillion dollars in ten years. Not only would this put them at or close to the top of all companies, in terms of total annual revenues, but they will also be sharing that grouping with companies like Amazon and Walmart that deliver on scale, but at the expense of margins, he said, adding that Anthropic emerges as a winner in the premium portion of the AI market, capturing a dominant market share, with pricing power.In his previous post valuing Anthropic, Damodaran had raised the alarm over the company’s governance structure, stating that its structure as a public benefit corporation and a voting share concoction that leaves founders in control, no matter how much capital the company raises in equity markets. He said he received feedback that this may not be a negative as these are smart people who know AI better than the rest. The analyst is however not convinced as he believes concentration of power in the hands of founders is a bad idea.Also read | Aswath Damodaran explains why country risk is no longer just an emerging market problem“While much of the focus on Anthropic has been on their compute commitments, disclosed (loosely) in their prospectus, my valuation of Anthropic is driven by expectations of what those commitments will look like over time, and especially if my growth story for the company comes into fruition. Delivering a trillion dollars of revenues will require Anthropic to not just maintain and replenish the compute power that it has already locked down, but add to that power over time,” Damodaran said, warning that building new data centers is getting more difficult, as local communities push back, and politicians realize that opposing them is a net vote winnerRegulatory risks are also one of the key worries for Anthropic. “Put simply, Anthropic will become riskier, if revenues do not measure up to expectations and the pathway to profitability becomes rockier, making it more an output than an input variable,” the valuation expert said.How investors should react to Anthropic’s IPO?While Damodaran remains cautious about Anthropic’s IPO, he noted that uncertainty is a feature of investing, no matter what one invests in, with the differences across investments lying in how much uncertainty one face, rather than whether she faces.Also read | AI boom heading for a dot-com-style bust? ‘Dean of Valuation’ Aswath Damodaran warns correction could be more painful than 2008He listed out four responses to such uncertainties.1) Ignore it: Damodaran pointed out that there are investors who are capable of ignoring uncertainty and going in fully even on the most uncertain investments. They are able to do so because they are far less risk averse than the rest and are willing to live with the consequences of investments (and their portfolios) blowing up. “They are more gamblers than investors, but with good instincts and timing, gamblers can get wealthy too,” he said.2) Avoid it: If an investor completely wants to avoid uncertainty, she cannot invest in equities, corporate bonds, which have risk of default, and even treasury bonds, which have price risk from shifting interest rates, Damodaran noted. Unless the investor simply wants to just hold cash, she has to therefore decide what her threshold for risk is, and stay within that threshold.3) Margin of Safety: The third approach to dealing with uncertainty also borrows from conventional value investing and imposing a margin of safety, where you will buy a stock only if its price is less than your value estimate by a margin (20%, 30%, 40%) that you specify.4) Law of large numbers: “If I had a million dollars in investable funds, would I invest that entire amount in Anthropic, even if it trades at well below my assessed value? The answer would be no, given the uncertainties associated with the future of the company, but that answer would change if my portfolio became less concentrated, since its performance would be less a function of any individual company's performance (good or bad),” Damodaran said. In effect, he said he is using the law of large numbers as an ally to not only reduce his risk exposure to individual companies, but also as a basis for making investments in far riskier stocks than he would be otherwise inclined to invest in.Disclaimer: This article has been written by Debaroti Adhikary, who is not a SEBI-registered Research Analyst or an Investment Adviser. items.summary: BSE on Wednesday reported a 44.9% year-on-year rise in consolidated net profit to Rs 809.15 crore for the second quarter of FY27 (Q2FY27), compared with Rs 558.43 crore in the corresponding period last year (Q2FY26).The exchange's revenue for the quarter increased 34.1% to Rs 1,432.6 crore from Rs 1,068.4 crore a year ago.Earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) rose 42.4% year-on-year to Rs 984 crore, compared with Rs 690.9 crore in the year-ago quarter.EBITDA margin expanded to 68.7% from 64.66% in the corresponding quarter last year.Transaction charges rose 42% year-on-year to Rs 1,127.8 crore in Q2FY27 from Rs 794 crore in Q2FY26.Treasury income on clearing and settlement funds declined 14% to Rs 36.5 crore from Rs 42.8 crore reported in the year-ago period.BSE's total operating expenses increased 21% year-on-year to Rs 494.7 crore in Q2FY27 from Rs 410.1 crore in Q2FY26.On a standalone basis, BSE's net profit after tax rose 50.3% year-on-year to Rs 773.4 crore in Q2FY27 from Rs 514.5 crore in the corresponding quarter of FY26. Revenue from operations increased 38.3% to Rs 1,349.3 crore from Rs 975.5 crore in Q2FY26.Board approves appointment of Ashutosh Singh as executive directorThe board of directors has approved the appointment of Ashutosh Singh (DIN: 10579541) as Executive Director – Business (Vertical 3) for a period of five years, effective November 30, 2026, subject to ratification of his appointment by the shareholders. The appointment follows the company's earlier intimations dated June 2, 2026, and October 21, 2026.The board has also approved a proposal to accept an offer from the Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority (MMRDA) for the allotment of a plot at Bandra Kurla Complex (BKC), Mumbai. The proposed plot will be used to develop additional premises and infrastructure facilities for the company. The transaction is subject to completion of the necessary documentation, fulfilment of applicable conditions and execution of definitive agreements with MMRDA.BSE's top shareholdersAs of September 2026, the Life Insurance Corporation of India was BSE's largest shareholder, with a 4.44% stake, followed by ICICI Prudential Focus Equity Fund at 2.70% and SBI Nifty 50 ETF at 2.57%.Nippon Life India Trustee Ltd – A/c Nippon India Growth Fund held a 1.84% stake, while Siddharth Balachandran owned 1.64%. Kotak Flexicap Fund held 1.52%, followed by Tata AIA Life Insurance Co Ltd – Whole Life Mid Cap at 1.42%. Invesco India Mid Cap Fund held a 1.25% stake, UTI Nifty 50 ETF owned 1.22%, while S Gopalakrishnan held 1.17%.BSE share priceAhead of its Q2 results announcement, BSE shares settled 1.75% lower at Rs 3,601.50 on the NSE, against the previous closing price. The stock has a 52-week trading range of Rs 2,377 to Rs 4,447, while its year-to-date return stood at 37%.BSE had a market capitalisation of Rs 1,46,899 crore on the NSE, as of November 4.

items.title: US: What happens next as Dems take over
items.summary: Washington: Democrats are preparing a legislative offensive against US President Donald Trump after their sweeping midterm victory handed them control of both chambers of Congress and the power to challenge his policies, investigate his administration and block his nominees.Emboldened by victories deep in traditional Republican territory, the party is promising swift action on living costs and the war in Iran, while signaling that investigations of alleged abuses and corruption will be a major priority.Also read | Did Iran war just blow up in Trump's face?House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries, who is in line to become the first Black speaker when the new Congress takes office in January, vowed to go after what he described as "unprecedented corruption" in the government."Because if you have people in high office who are so focused on enriching themselves, their family members, their friends, or their donors, then they're not focused on making life better for the American people," he said.But Democrats will not have a free hand. Trump retains his veto, while Senate rules allow Republicans to obstruct most legislation.Here are the opportunities -- and obstacles -- ahead.First 100 hoursJeffries has promised an ambitious legislative push in the House's first 100 hours, focused on affordability -- the issue that dominated an election shaped by tariffs, high prices and the Iran war.His priorities include restoring expired Affordable Care Act health insurance subsidies, reversing nearly $1 trillion in Medicaid cuts enacted under Trump, rolling back tariffs and pressing for an end to the conflict, which has sent fuel costs soaring.With majorities in both chambers, Democrats can bring their proposals to votes and take charge of spending negotiations. They could use federal budget deadlines to demand concessions, although confrontations over spending risk government shutdowns.'Lawyer up'Oversight may offer an even more immediate means of challenging Trump.Robert Garcia, the Democrat expected to chair the powerful House Oversight Committee, fired off a blunt election-night message to Republicans on social media: "LAWYER UP."Also read | What Trump & Republicans' loss means for IndiaOregon Senator Ron Wyden was even more concise, posting a single word: "Subpoenas."With control of committees in both chambers, Democrats can summon officials, demand documents and hold public hearings, potentially putting Trump and his senior aides under intense scrutiny.Likely subjects include the Trump family's business and cryptocurrency dealings, government contracts involving billionaire Elon Musk, cuts to federal agencies, immigration enforcement and the conduct of the Iran war.Democrats have also signaled interest in the handling of files relating to notorious sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.The administration could resist demands for testimony or documents, triggering court battles.Democrats could pursue Trump's third impeachment, though party leaders have not committed to doing so. The House needs only a simple majority to impeach, but removing a president requires a two-thirds vote in the Senate -- far beyond the party's numbers.Senate muscleThe Senate majority gives Democrats another powerful lever: control of confirmations.They can block Trump's judicial and cabinet nominees, including any selection to fill a Supreme Court vacancy, potentially curbing his influence over the courts long after he leaves office.Also read | Vivek Ramaswamy: Decoding a Republican firebrand's high-decibel fallDemocratic Senate chairs will also decide which bills and investigations receive committee attention.Limits and dealsPassing laws will be much harder than launching investigations.Most legislation must clear a 60-vote hurdle in the Senate to overcome procedural obstruction. Trump can veto bills passed by Congress, and overturning a veto requires two-thirds support in both chambers.He also retains substantial executive powers over immigration, trade and military operations, although lawmakers can seek to constrain them through legislation and spending decisions.Trump struck a conciliatory note after the rout, praising Democrats for doing a "good job" and telling The New York Times that he would accept the result and expected to work with them.He even raised the possibility of cooperation on immigration.But he had previously warned that if Democrats won Congress, "I veto everything" -- a reminder that the next two years could be defined as much by confrontation as compromise.

items.title: Cabinet clears ₹14,500 cr funding scheme for battery energy storage systems
items.summary:
The Union Cabinet on Wednesday approved Rs 14,500 crore in viability gap funding for 92 GWh of grid-scale energy storage systems between FY27 and FY31.
This development is significant given India's ambitious target of 500 GW of renewable energy by 2030.
The scheme is aimed at supporting the development of 92 GWh storage capacity across three technologies -- Battery Energy Storage System (30 GWh), Pumped Storage Projects (60 GWh) and Emerging Storage Technologies (2GW), Information and Broadcasting Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said in a media briefing here.
The minister said the scheme will be implemented for five years till 2030-31.

The Odisha government has submitted a proposal to the Centre for setting up 290 additional public electric vehicle (EV) charging stations in 13 cities across the state under the PM E-DRIVE scheme, officials said on Wednesday.
The proposal has been submitted under the direction of Commerce and Transport Minister Bibhuti Bhushan Jena as part of the state's efforts to strengthen EV infrastructure, they said.
In the first phase of the scheme, the Centre has approved the setting up of 170 EV charging stations in seven major cities, and work on the project is currently underway, an official statement said.
In the second phase, the state has proposed setting up 290 additional public charging stations in Rourkela, Talcher, Sambalpur, Paradip, Barbil, Balpahad, Berhampur, Brajarajnagar, Chhatrapur, Jharsuguda, Joda, Keonjhar and Rajgangpur, besides locations along various national and state highways.

items.title: Govt approves strengthening of fast track courts to deal with child abuse
items.summary:
The Union Cabinet on Wednesday approved the strengthening and extension of 850 fast track courts to deal with child abuse and rape cases, Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said.
Briefing reporters on decisions taken by the Cabinet, Vaishnaw said the Modi government is committed to firmly dealing with cases of atrocities against women and children.
He said the decision is part of efforts to fully utilise and implement prevailing laws and draft new legislations to deal with such cases.
The Centrally Sponsored Scheme for the establishment of Fast Track Special Courts (FTSCs), including exclusive POCSO (ePOCSO) courts, was introduced in October 2019, following the enactment of the Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2018 and the order of the Supreme Court.
These courts are dedicated to the time-bound trial and disposal of pending cases related to rape and crimes under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012.

In this Diwali special of the Moneycontrol Wealth Formula podcast, market veteran Sanjoy Bhattacharyya of Fortuna Capital joins Mahalakshmi for a deep-dive into how investors should navigate this phase. With over three decades of experience, Sanjoy shares his investment philosophy and explains why surviving difficult markets matters more than chasing spectacular returns. In this conversation: Why high valuations and a flood of IPOs have weighed on market returns Why investing is 85–90% temperament and only 10–15% intellect How to identify businesses that can deliver sustainable growth without excessive capital The biggest warning signs: weak management, poor governance, debt and related-party transactions When a sharp fall in a stock is an opportunity — and when it is a warning Why investors must reassess their losers and learn to cut their losses The dangers of FOMO, overconfidence and trying to get rich quickly Why the best way to build wealth is to think like a businessman and own enduring businesses Sanjay also discusses investment lessons from companies such as IEX, Kingfa, Laurus Labs and Infosys. The big takeaway: Don't chase the market. Protect your capital, stay patient and focus on owning good businesses. items.title: Will Republicans learn from this defeat?
items.summary: A healthy Republican Party would respond to this historic midterm-election repudiation of President Donald Trump with contrition and honest introspection. Its leaders would plot a fresh path forward and shed the elements of a White House agenda that drove American voters to hand control of the House of Representatives and US Senate to a Democratic Party they don’t even approve of all that much.Reduced to a rump in Congress and its governing coalition gutted to the bone — just in time for 2028 — that Republican Party would assemble a more durable confederation of voters that doesn’t rise and fall on the whims of a narcissistic albeit once-in-a-generation political talent.But Republicans and their exalted leader aren’t the picture of political health.Those within the party most likely to confront reality and take on the difficult work of rebuilding the GOP were cut down in ruby-red House districts, Senate seats and governors’ mansions that have simply not elected Democrats. The only Republicans left standing were insulated — by gerrymandered districts, their constituents’ stubborn support for Trump or a combination of the two. The party’s short-sighted motivation will be to follow the president’s defiant lead and resist the new Democratic majorities’ attempts to neuter the commander-in-chief.And so the party’s future, immediate and otherwise, is in Trump’s hands, and most elected officials would still take their cues from the White House.As the shocking returns flowed in showing defeats in Senate contests in Iowa, Kansas, Ohio, South Carolina and Texas (Texas!), some veteran party insiders I spoke with disagreed with my assessment and argued that battered congressional Republicans would be chastened, distance themselves from Trump and finally end blind support for his agenda on Capitol Hill. Some Republican operatives even speculated that Vice President JD Vance would be forced to abandon any plans he might have to seek the White House, to say nothing of aspiring Cabinet members.I’m not a gambler. But if I were, I wouldn’t risk a nickel on that bet. The siren song of the president’s loyal, Make American Great Again (MAGA) populist base will be hard for the party’s 2028 contenders to resist — and that’s if a major effort materializes to wean the party off of Trump.This isn’t the first time the president has led his party into a ditch, only to recover like Lazarus because he refused to concede failure. That kind of obstinance inspires grassroots conservatives who see a fighter rather than a shirker. “I wasn’t on the ballot and if I was, we would have won IN A LANDSLIDE!” Trump said in a Truth Social post on election night. Meanwhile, GOP strategists told me with a high degree of confidence that Democrats will overplay their hand — just like Republicans did — causing voters to turn back to Trump and the GOP just in time for a presidential campaign now unexpectedly ripe with opportunity.The claim that Democrats will overreach and offer Republicans a chance to revive their political standing is not unreasonable; the US has seen both political parties misinterpret an election backlash. The Democrats did so following back-to-back blue waves in 2006 and 2008. Two years later in 2010, a red wave gained the GOP 63 House districts and seven Senate seats during President Barack Obama’s first midterm election. The Republicans committed the same faux pas during Trump’s first presidency, which fueled a blue wave-flip of 41 House districts in the 2018 midterm election.No doubt, if Democrats dive head first into impeaching Trump and legislate on culture-war issues after the new Congress is seated in January, voters will sour on them rather quickly. But I wonder if Republicans have digested the breadth of the destruction the 45th and 47th president left in his wake this week — an apocalyptic political disaster that, as polling analyst Sean Trende points out, hasn’t been seen since 1974, in the aftermath of the Watergate scandal that left the GOP on life support.Republicans didn’t just lose a Senate seat in Kansas for the first time in nearly a century. The Democrats were possibly poised to win a Senate seat in Mississippi for the first time since 1982. The GOP lost states, districts and other offices that Trump and his GOP predecessors have been carrying by double digits going back years, if not decades. That outcome demands a wholesale reevaluation of American politics and the blue-state, red-state paradigm the US has lived under for a quarter century.Trump doesn’t seem much interested in doing so. And if past is prologue, that means Republicans won’t be either. They might need to lose some more, first.

Indian-American Vivek Ramaswamy, who was backed by US President Donald Trump, lost Ohio's gubernatorial race to Democrat Amy Acton.
Ramaswamy, 41, lost to 60-year-old Acton, who became the first woman to be elected governor of the state.
Acton bagged over 51 per cent of the votes while Ramaswamy won over 45 per cent.
In concession remarks in Ohio after losing the governor's race, Ramaswamy said: "It was a tough race. It was bitter at times in both directions... All of us in this room should be rooting for the success of her administration," C-SPAN quoted him as saying.
The billionaire also thanked his parents, his wife and her parents for their support.
Ramaswamy lost despite having top strategists from his and Vice President JD Vance's political teams advising him, NBC News reported.

items.title: Trump accepts defeat, hints at future role as ‘pundit’
Decoding a Rep firebrand's high-decibel fall
items.summary: Vivek Ramaswamy's meteoric rise was built on the promise that an outsider equipped with sharp rhetoric, business credentials and unwavering loyalty to Donald Trump could reshape the fortunes of the Republican Party. His defeat in Ohio at the US midterms today could be proof that national-level visibility, proximity to the president and political acumen may not be enough to convert big political fame into a poll success story.Democrat Amy Acton defeated the Trump-backed Ramaswamy in the Ohio governor's race, ending Republican control of the state governor office and delivering Democrats their first victory in the contest in 20 years.Also read | US has no immediate plan to strike Iran, Trump tells FTJust ahead of the vote, Ramaswamy drew public attention in stunning fashion by bringing out a highly controversial ad based on an episode from Acton's personal life. The ad eventually went on to divide opinions like few other ads in recent memory.As Ramaswamy's camapaign for the high-profile seat got progressively heated up, Trump and Vice-President JD Vance repeatedly travelled to Ohio to campaign for him.The win for Acton, who also became the first woman elected governor of Ohio, came despite more than $100 million being spent against her on the strength of substantial financial backing from Ramaswamy's allies.Decoding a high-profile lossRamaswamy's defeat is significant because he was more than an ordinary Republican gubernatorial candidate. The biotech entrepreneur had emerged as one of the most recognisable faces of the party's new generation, using television debates, social media and provocative political arguments to build a national following.His 2021 bestseller Woke, Inc. helped establish his credentials as an anti-woke conservative. During the 2024 Republican presidential primaries, his combative debate performances and uncompromising positions attracted considerable attention, even though he eventually finished fourth in the Iowa caucuses before withdrawing and endorsing Trump.Also read | 'We would have won a landslide': Trump claims Republicans would have won big if on ballotHis political ascent also earned him a brief role alongside Elon Musk in the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE).His ability to articulate the MAGA movement's positions with unusual energy made him an influential political communicator. He also helped broaden the Republican Party's appeal by demonstrating that its conservative nationalist message could be championed by an Indian-American Hindu.His defeat is now raising questions about whether national fame can translate into support at the state level.The limits of MAGAFor Trump, the result could be a marked setback. Ramaswamy had the president's backing, substantial campaign resources and support from prominent Republicans. These big advantages, however, failed to overcome voter concerns about affordability, rising living costs and fuel prices.Acton, on the other hands, made these issues central to her campaign, which likely played a huge role in giving her the win.Ramaswamy's loss also might go on to show that Trump's political influence has limits, particularly when voters are focused on other important issues.The ad featuring Acton's estranged mother may have added a major layer of complication to Ramaswamy's campaign. The advertisement divided opinions sharply and drew fierce criticism from both Republicans and Democrats.Trump publicly defended Ramaswamy's ad and his decision to run it. It probably turned out to be one of the factors that backfired on their high-decibel campaign, with voters taking strong issue with a move made in bad taste.No country for loud menFor Republicans, Ohio may have just offered a warning -- that political savvy, money & fundraising muscle and sleek rhetoric don't guarantee a win.For Ramaswamy, this defeat does not diminish him or erode his ability to shape conservative debates. What it actually does is, it exposes the gap between being a MAGA bigshot and turning that into a poll win.Some analysts also said this loss might also toughen things for new Republican faces hoping to inherit Trump's legacy. Ramaswamy had positioned himself as a flagbearer of that generation. His fall may have just suggested that the party's future will depend not just on sharp rhetoric and money power, but also on how it addresses actual socio-economic issues.

items.title: DDCA seeks venue change for India-Sri Lanka ODI over pollution concerns
items.summary:
The opening One-Day International between India and Sri Lanka slated to be played in the national capital on December 13 is likely to be moved out due to pollution and outfield revamp.
With pollution at its peak in the months of November and December being a major factor, the Delhi and District Cricket Association has requested the BCCI to move the game out of Delhi also because of the outfield work currently underway at the Feroz Shah Kotla.
A sand-based outfield is being laid and the work will go on for the next three months.
"Pollution is a major factor and then there is renovation work going on. So we have requested the BCCI to move the game out of Delhi," a DDCA source told PTI.
India and Sri Lanka are scheduled to play three ODIs and as many T20Is in December.

items.title: Rupee rises 14 paise to 94.61 against US dollar during early trade
items.summary:
The rupee strengthened by 14 paise to 94.61 against the US dollar in early trade on Wednesday, supported by receding crude oil prices, a weaker US dollar and inflows of foreign funds.
Buying momentum in the domestic equities market also favoured the Indian currency even as investors awaited the outcome of the US midterm elections, according to forex traders.

items.title: Explained: Why Sebi wants mutual fund investors to switch to direct plans
items.summary: Sebi has directed mutual fund houses to make direct plans the default option on their digital platforms from 1st November. A look at the reason behind the regulator’s action.WHAT ARE DIRECT AND REGULAR PLANS IN MUTUAL FUNDS?Direct and regular plans are two ways of investing in a mutual fund scheme. In a direct plan, investors put money in a scheme without involving a distributor, broker or agent. Since no commission is paid, the scheme’s expense ratio or fee is lower.A regular plan is bought through a distributor, broker or adviser. The mutual fund pays a commission to the intermediary, and this cost is recovered from the investor through the scheme’s expense ratio. As a result, the expense ratio is higher than that of direct plans.According to the latest AMFI data, the total expense ratio (TER) of regular plans ranges from 0.36% to 4.3%, compared with 0% to 2.7% for direct plans.WHAT HAS SEBI CHANGED AND WHY?From November 1, Sebi has asked mutual fund houses to make direct plans the default option on their websites and mobile apps. So, if an investor visits a fund house’s app to invest in an equity scheme, the direct plan will now be pre-selected or displayed as the primary option. Investors can still choose regular plans if they want distributor assistance.Read more: Sebi levies Rs 40 lakh penalty on four entities in Axis MF front-running caseBUT WHAT’S WRONG WITH REGULAR PLANS?There is nothing wrong per se with regular plans. In fact, it may be suitable for investors seeking professional guidance or those new to mutual funds. After all, distributors handle the client portfolios and do periodic reviews of the holdings.But, critics point out that in addition to the higher costs, regular plans could result in conflict of interest. Since distributors are paid commissions by fund houses, this would push some intermediaries to recommend schemes that offer higher commissions rather than those best suited for client needs. They claim investors would be better off availing the services of fee-based financial advisers, who charge investors directly for their advice.HOW MUCH MONEY CAN INVESTORS SAVE THROUGH LOWER EXPENSE RATIOS?While the difference in the total expense ratio may appear small, it can significantly impact returns over long investment horizons.For instance, an investor putting Rs 20,000 a month into an equity mutual fund for 15 years, assuming annual returns of 12%, could accumulate around Rs 94.4 lakh in a direct plan with a 0.7% expense ratio. In comparison, the corpus would be about Rs 86 lakh in a regular plan with a 1.7% expense ratio.The difference arises because lower expenses leave more money invested, allowing returns to compound over time.Read more: Quant Mutual Fund reduces exposure to frontline IT stocks as part of profit-booking exerciseWHO SHOULD CONSIDER DIRECT PLANS?Direct plans are suitable for investors who can research funds, monitor their portfolios and make investment decisions independently or with the help of fee-based advisors.If you understand concepts such as asset allocation, risk management and portfolio rebalancing, and can stay invested through market cycles, a direct plan may be a good option.

'Tesla misled South Korean customers'
items.summary: Tesla has misled tens of thousands of South Korean customers by marketing driver-assistance software that the company knows cannot be legally used in most of its vehicles in the country, according to a complaint an advocacy group plans to file with a consumer protection agency on Thursday.Tesla has marketed Full Self-Driving (Supervised) software to prospective buyers in South Korea for years, often collecting lump-sum payments of 9.043 million won ($6,726).FSD can be used on about 20% of Tesla vehicles registered in South Korea - those manufactured in the US, Tesla Korea country manager Seo Young-deuk said in parliamentary testimony last month. Those cars meet US vehicle-safety standards that South Korea recognizes as part of a free trade agreement, according to the forthcoming complaint to the Korea Fair Trade Commission (KFTC), seen by Reuters.The complaint to the regulator, which also handles antitrust, has not been previously reported.Most Tesla vehicles in South Korea, however, are manufactured in China, where no such agreement exists. Tesla only recently started the process for obtaining FSD certification for China-made vehicles, despite charging customers for the software for more than three years.SOUTH KOREAN TRADE COMMISSION INVESTIGATINGIt is unclear how many South Korean customers purchased FSD subscriptions on ineligible vehicles, but Tesla has sold more than 170,000 Shanghai-produced vehicles in South Korea since 2023, according to Tesla data sent to South Korea's National Assembly."Tesla generated substantial revenue by selling an expensive driver-assistance system to mass-market buyers who cannot use it for even a single day," said Choi Young-suk, who leads automotive issues at the advocacy group Citizens United for Consumer Sovereignty.Tesla did not respond to requests for comment. A KFTC official said the agency launched a probe earlier this year into Tesla's advertising of its FSD system and has received written responses from the company, but declined to provide further details.Tesla continued to market FSD as sales of ineligible China-manufactured Teslas surged in South Korea in recent years. Sales of FSD-incompatible Teslas made in China grew more than fivefold in South Korea from 2023 through last year, when 99% of new Teslas sold in South Korea could not legally use FSD, according to data Tesla submitted to the National Assembly.Despite years of promises from CEO Elon Musk that all Teslas would soon become fully driverless vehicles, FSD is not autonomous and requires active human supervision.Tesla has sought to expand FSD's reach beyond North America, particularly in Europe, where the company has waged a pressure campaign against European regulators.TESLA SALES SURGE IN SOUTH KOREATesla surpassed BMW this year as South Korea's top imported-car brand, according to South Korean import data.Tesla sold FSD for one-time payments for years, before shifting to a monthly subscription of 150,000 won ($112) in August.The complaint alleges that Tesla promoted FSD last year as "coming soon" and posted a demonstration video filmed in South Korea without clearly disclosing that the technology could only be used in a small fraction of Teslas being sold.Tesla knew those limitations but continued to market the software to all customers, the complaint said.Tesla Korea manager Seo testified during an October 8 parliamentary hearing that the company had not formally requested FSD testing from the transport ministry. Two weeks later, Tesla applied for certification.The ministry said FSD does not comply with local safety rules, including requirements for drivers to keep their hands on the wheel, according to a statement it sent to a lawmaker, reviewed by Reuters. The transport ministry could not be reached for comment.The consumer group accused Tesla Korea of deceptive marketing and asked the KFTC to issue a temporary cease-and-desist order on marketing FSD for ineligible vehicles, impose administrative fines and refer the case to state investigators.

items.title: China curbs cloud SK Hynix’s NY chip plans
items.summary: US officials have held up approval for American chipmaking equipment needed by SK Hynix to expand production in China, complicating the South Korean chipmaker's plans for new memory-chip plants in New York, according to people familiar with the matter.SK Hynix is seeking US export licenses to equip its Dalian plant, arguing that increased production there would help fund its planned US expansion. But the Commerce Department has yet to approve the new licenses, the people said.Its Solidigm unit plans to invest about $45 billion and build two NAND plants in Marcy, New York, two people said, with investment potentially reaching about $100 billion over time. NAND is memory that retains data even when power is turned off and is used for storage in data centers.Also Read | Samsung to make AMD, Nvidia chip parts at second Texas plant: ReportTRUMP ADMINISTRATION FACES POLICY DILEMMAThe negotiations raise questions about how far the Trump administration is willing to bend national security guardrails established to keep US technology from aiding China's military, in order to bring foreign investment and chipmaking onshore."Ultimately, none of this is going to go forward without a green light from the White House," said Leland Miller, a member of the US-China Economic and Security Review Commission, a bipartisan panel created by the US Congress. The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment.Negotiations are continuing, the people said, with approval for the Dalian expansion central to SK Hynix's plans in New York.Also Read | Japan to invest up to $21 billion in two US chip factories to be run by GlobalFoundriesCOMMERCE DEPARTMENT MEETINGS INTENSIFYExecutives from SK Hynix's US subsidiary, Solidigm, have met nearly 10 times with officials from the Commerce Department since late August, one of the people said. The company needs to ramp up production and develop more sophisticated NAND chipmaking in China to generate revenue to build a US facility and to stay competitive, the people said.In a meeting last week, Commerce Under Secretary Jeffrey Kessler held to his position that the US would not allow more American chipmaking tools to upgrade or expand capacity, the person said, though the department has not formally denied a license to export American equipment to fill empty clean space in Dalian. The two sides are also negotiating a separate license for 2027 for equipment to keep up the Dalian facility, the person said.A spokesperson for the Department of Commerce did not immediately respond to a request for comment.In a statement last week, Solidigm said: "As a US-founded and headquartered company, Solidigm regularly evaluates strategic alternatives to best serve its customers and enhance its long-term competitiveness. The company is currently exploring options for building a NAND memory fab at potential locations around the world. No decision regarding any specific course of action has been made." Solidigm stuck to its statement from last week. SK Hynix did not immediately respond to a request for comment outside business hours.

items.title: IDBI Bank Strike: What's on November 10?
items.summary: A two-day nationwide strike by IDBI Bank officers and employees against the proposed sale of a majority stake in the lender to Canada's Fairfax Financial Holdings ended on Tuesday. The employees' union will decide its next course of action at a meeting on November 10 as it continues to oppose the disinvestment. The strike was called by the United Forum of IDBI Officers and Employees, which is seeking to stop the proposed transaction. The union said the protest received a strong response from employees and officers across the country."The strike got a massive response from employees and officers across the country. We will decide the future course of action in our core committee meeting post Diwali on November 10 on the way to intensify struggle," United Forum of IDBI Officers and Employees convener Devidas Tuljapurkar said.Read more - Get ready to pay double for parking in Delhi: MCD plans to hike charges at 400 parking lots under GRAP-II; what two-wheeler and car owners need to knowHe added that the union would approach the United Forum of Bank Unions (UFBU) to seek wider support, including the possibility of a nationwide bank strike.IDBI Bank employees oppose proposed stake sale to FairfaxThe union has raised concerns about the valuation of the lender and the possibility of its assets and business capabilities being undervalued in the transaction."We are seriously concerned that the transaction may undervalue IDBI’s properties, institutional capabilities, customer relationships, future earnings and strategic importance," Tuljapurkar said.Read more - Rahul Gandhi vs Narendra Modi debate: RaGa asks public if they want open face-off; urges Nitin Gadkari, Yogi Adityanath & other BJP leaders to convince PMHe also called on the government to make the valuation process more transparent. The union wants the government to disclose the valuation methodology, the assumptions used, how real estate and other assets have been assessed, and the reasons for accepting the proposed sale price.Tuljapurkar said the public should have clear evidence that a national asset was not being transferred at a throwaway price. He also called for scrutiny of the proposed buyer's ownership structure, financial position, regulatory record and any substantiated controversies in its home jurisdiction.Congress calls IDBI Bank disinvestment a 'scam'The proposed sale has also drawn criticism from the Opposition. The Congress on Monday described the IDBI Bank disinvestment as a 'scam' and demanded that the government stop the sale to a foreign company and set up a Joint Parliamentary Committee (JPC) to investigate the process.Congress general secretary in-charge of communications Jairam Ramesh alleged that a foreign company was acquiring the lender using funds belonging to the bank itself."This is yet another major scam by the Modi government, which warrants an investigation. We demand that the process of selling IDBI Bank to a foreign company be halted," Ramesh said in a post on X.IDBI Bank stake sale: Government, LIC to sell 60.72% stakeThe Central government on October 14 approved the sale of a combined 60.72% stake in IDBI Bank to Fairfax Financial Holdings for around Rs 53,000 crore (USD 5.5 billion).Under the proposed transaction, Fairfax will acquire the government's 30.48% stake, valued at around Rs 26,620 crore, and LIC's 30.24% holding, worth approximately Rs 26,440 crore.The Canadian billionaire Prem Watsa-led Fairfax will pay Rs 81 per share, above the benchmark fair value of Rs 75.99 determined by two independent valuation agencies.The deal, if completed, would mark one of the largest foreign investments in an Indian bank and a major step in the country's long-delayed banking privatisation programme.The Central government currently holds 45.48% of IDBI Bank, while LIC owns 49.24%. The transaction is expected to be completed by the end of the current financial year, subject to regulatory clearance from the Reserve Bank of India (RBI).How many employees does IDBI Bank have?IDBI Bank has 19,108 employees on its rolls, including 9,500 employees from Scheduled Caste, Scheduled Tribe and Other Backward Classes categories.The lender also has 6,911 women employees and 884 employees with disabilities. The proposed stake sale has therefore become a major concern for the employees' union, which is seeking clarity on the transaction and its implications.Inputs from PTI

items.title: US job openings increase by 333,000 in Sept
items.summary: WASHINGTON, - US job openings increased sharply in September while layoffs fell, supporting economists' views that the labor market remained on firmer footing despite tepid employment gains during that month.Job openings, a measure of labor demand, had risen by 333,000 to 7.523 million by the last day of September, the Labor Department's Bureau of Labor Statistics said in its Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey, or JOLTS report, on Tuesday. Data for August was revised slightly higher to show 7.190 million vacancies instead of the previously reported 7.079 million.Click here to track US midterm election results 2026 live updates Economists polled by Reuters had forecast 7.100 million unfilled positions in September. The job openings rate rose to 4.5% from 4.3% in August. The JOLTS report has been plagued by a low response rate, which has decreased considerably from the period prior to the COVID-19 pandemic.Economists view the labor market as continuing to be in a "low-hire, low-fire" state, and argue that strong profits as domestic demand remains resilient were keeping layoffs near historic lows. The ongoing US-Israeli war with Iran is, however, making employers hesitant to boost hiring, they said.Hiring increased by 131,000 to 5.402 million in September. The hires rate rose to 3.4% from 3.3% in August. Layoffs and discharges decreased by 127,000 to 1.641 million, with the rate falling to 1.0% from 1.1% in August.Nonfarm payrolls increased by 29,000 jobs in September. A Reuters survey of economists expects payrolls to have advanced by 65,000 in October. The unemployment rate is forecast to have been unchanged at 4.2%.

items.title: TaMo-Iveco to create world's 4th largest CV group with ₹2.28 trn revenue
items.summary:
Tata Motors and Italy-headquartered Iveco on Tuesday announced that the combined enterprise will be the world's fourth-largest commercial vehicle maker with a revenue of Rs 2.28 lakh crore (Euro 21 billion).
The Indian auto major acquired an 89.42 per cent stake in Iveco for nearly 3.43 billion euros post the initial settlement of its cash tender offer, even as the buyout continues.
The acquisition of Iveco, making it an indirect subsidiary of the Indian auto major, will be Tata Motors' biggest since it bought Jaguar Land Rover from Ford in 2008. Iveco Group employs 33,000 people and operates 16 industrial sites and 22 R&D centres.
The settlement follows the completion of the acceptance period of the voluntary tender offer, under which Tata Motors offered EUR 14.4 per share in cash for Iveco's common shares.
